items.title: The Magician
items.short: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission
meaning: The first arcanum in the destiny matrix is The Magician, the energy of pure will and of beginning. If a one came up in your calculation, this is a person who works as a source: they do not wait for circumstances to line up, they take what is at hand and set things moving themselves. “One” here is read literally — it is the point where everything only starts, not yet split into doubts, for and against.

As a number of destiny, one is about authorship. Its bearer is not satisfied with taking part: it matters to them to put their own name on the result and to see a mark in the world that would not be there without them. This is the active, “daytime” side of the matrix — not storing up, but showing; not waiting for a sign, but making the first move. Hence the character of the energy: direct, impatient, turned outwards.

On the tarot card, The Magician stands at a table with the symbols of all the elements and joins “above” and “below” with a single gesture. This is the image of a conductor: an idea turns into a thing directly, through the hand and the will, with no go-betweens and no long approvals. Being the first arcanum feels like a steady inner itch of “just do it” — a quiet pressure that looks for a way out in a concrete move rather than in thinking about it.

Strong and weak versions are one energy turned in different directions. In the strong one the will goes into the object: a person makes what did not exist and measures themselves by what is done. In the weak one it turns back on the author — it matters more to feel capable than to carry an idea through to a thing, and the force leaks away into loud intentions and plans that never become a result. The difference is not in the amount of energy but in where the will points: at the work, or at the image of oneself.

Telling one apart from its neighbouring arcana is easiest by the direction of its force. The second arcanum, The High Priestess, carries force too, but the opposite kind: she knows and stays silent, gathers inside, waits for the right moment — while The Magician shows himself outwards and acts first. And from the eleventh, Strength, one is separated by distance: The Magician is good at the dash and at the start, Strength is good at holding out and finishing what was begun. The first arcanum is about taking something on, not about seeing it through to the end.

in_positions.character: The core of this character is the first step. The person takes hold of a task before everyone else has finished talking, and you can see at once that they will not ask for permission. Charm comes with the package, but it rests on results rather than on manners.
in_positions.comfort: What refills this centre is action, not quiet: an hour spent on something new gives back more strength than a whole free day. An empty evening with no tasks does not restore this centre, it irritates it — here a change of occupation is what works as rest.
in_positions.profession: A talent for starting things and explaining them. The best fit is work that has to be raised from zero: the first sales, a new direction, a course written from a blank page. Long upkeep of something already built suffocates this person, and they leave such a job within a year. This talent needs a short run-up with one measurable result — the point after which an idea has become a working launch.
in_positions.realisation: Realisation goes through projects of your own. Inside somebody else’s structure everything still works out, yet the feeling of “this is not mine” never passes. A business of your own is not a whim here, it is the way to live long enough to see a result.
in_positions.karma40: After forty the lens of the first arcanum tests the ability to finish. Starting comes to this arcanum from birth, while holding focus to the end has to be learned through abandoned projects, every one of which looked good at the start.
in_positions.resources: Resources come in through initiative: called first, offered first, named the price first. Waiting to be noticed makes no sense here — movement begins with an action and stops the moment the person goes quiet.
in_positions.family_gifts: The family line passed down the ability to start with nothing to lean on. Most likely there was someone who left for another city with a single suitcase, or opened a business first among everyone they knew and asked nobody for permission. What is inherited is not their route but the right to take the first step before everything is ready.
in_positions.soul_tasks: Inner work here is about the honesty of the tool. The ability to influence unfolds into manipulation very easily, and only the person themselves can tell the two apart. The question is simple: did people feel lighter after the conversation, or did the speaker just get what they came for.
in_positions.past_lives: The karmic tail drags along the habit of starting first and dropping things halfway. Starting from zero is already worked through: this person gets a venture going where others are still getting ready. The thrill leaves together with the novelty, and a dozen beginnings pile up behind, not one of them carried to the end. Take a single thing already begun to its first measurable result, and only then pick up something new.
in_positions.purpose: Purpose here is tied to beginnings: opening what does not exist yet and passing the tool on. It does not have to be a business — a school, a method, a workshop. What matters is that a working arrangement is left behind after the person.
in_positions.money: Money comes for speed and for a direct offer. Short deals, projects of your own and payment for results all work well here. A fixed salary with a promotion somewhere ahead kills the pace: with no movement the income stands still. Say the price and the deadline out loud to one person, before you agree to work “as a trial”.
in_positions.money40: Mature money for the first arcanum rests on a name rather than on speed. There are fewer sprints, and the entry price is higher: the record already shows that this person finishes what they begin. That price drops when the record is twenty things started and abandoned — then every new start is counted from zero again. Write down three pieces of work carried to the end over the last five years and set the price from those, not from a readiness to take on anything at all.
in_positions.relations: Into a couple this brings initiative and excitement: courts fast, decides fast, gets bored just as fast. The bond stays alive only where there is a shared undertaking and shared plans, not habit alone. Silent waiting goes unread: until a request is said out loud, as far as they are concerned nothing is happening.
in_positions.parents_children: What was carried out of the family is the demand to cope alone, and early. Later the person leads younger ones like a coach: shows how it is done and expects independence ahead of time — with a child, a student or a newcomer on the team alike. Permission to do it their own way helps; endless comparison with a previous result gets in the way.
in_positions.ancestry: For the family line the task is to bring the family craft out of the shadows and into the open. The elders knew how but never dared to show it — hence the task of naming a price out loud and putting your own name on the work. Begin with one step: sign your name to work that the family used to hand over in silence.
in_positions.body_resource: When the work really grips them, The Magician easily forgets about pauses: a day flies past in one breath, and once the interest is gone even a simple task starts to drag. At their best, such a person breaks off the sprint in the middle of the excitement: stood up, went out, will finish tomorrow — and the evening stays alive. The weak spot is the belief that interest replaces reserves: three weeks in one breath end in days when even answering messages will not move. It is useful to compare several weeks by one marker: how much of what was begun got finished without dropping out of everything afterwards.
in_positions.chakras: The Magician: at this level arcanum 1 gives its own thing — the ability to launch what does not exist yet. Out of balance it shows as scattering across ten started projects. The practical test of the level is to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.rest: Rest comes in the new, not in the quiet: a trip to an unfamiliar city, a course outside the profession, an evening with people who talk about their own work. A beach with no tasks lasts three days, after that they start inventing work for themselves. The sign of a good break is simple: afterwards you are drawn back to your own affairs, not to five new projects.
in_positions.loops: The repeating program is a dash and a collapse. The person takes a high pace, gets halfway, loses interest and explains it by circumstances. The way out is plain: set the finish line in advance and reach it once.
in_positions.years: A decade under The Magician is a time for starting: a change of city, of profession, a first project of your own, and whatever begins here picks up speed faster than in any other period. A start turns into a result when one of the things begun reaches its first real confirmation — a client, a diploma, a working launch. The weak spot of the stage is ten open directions and not one of them closed: all the force of the start goes into the start itself. Write out every direction begun and keep the one that already has a checkable result.
in_positions.day: Arcanum “The Magician” · A · The first impression is built around one theme: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. At its strongest the person moves from thought to action quickly; under strain they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. The image becomes a steady reputation when they manage to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.month: Arcanum “The Magician” · B · The inborn spiritual task switches on by itself: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. in_positions.year: Arcanum “The Magician” · C · The material task carries the theme of will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission, from plan into result. The strong side shows in practice: the person moves from thought to action quickly; out of balance they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. This position is lived not by a promise but by the readiness to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.mission: Arcanum “The Magician” · D · This is not a punishment but a story that keeps coming back: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. The grown-up answer begins where the person moves from thought to action quickly, and the old circle begins with the opposite: they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. A concrete decision breaks the repeat — pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.center: Arcanum “The Magician” · E · At the centre of the chart it is easier to be yourself through this theme: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. Coming back to yourself takes action rather than distraction — pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.father_line: Arcanum “The Magician” · F · The spiritual male line keeps one principle: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. The strong side of the inheritance looks like this: the person moves from thought to action quickly; the heavy side of the script is dropping things halfway once the thrill is gone. Taking the force of the line without its hardness means picking one thing and taking it to the first result.
in_positions.mother_line: Arcanum “The Magician” · G · The spiritual female line keeps a house rule: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. In its supporting version the person moves from thought to action quickly; in its tangled version they repeat something else — dropping things halfway once the thrill is gone. Rewriting the rule while keeping its value comes down to a choice: pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.descendants: Arcanum “The Magician” · H · Here the family principle turns into a deed: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. In its reliable form the person moves from thought to action quickly; the automatic form drops things halfway once the thrill is gone. A new continuation of the male line begins with the ability to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.inheritance: Arcanum “The Magician” · I · Here the values of the family line enter everyday life: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. The resource shows when the person moves from thought to action quickly; the usual tilt is dropping things halfway once the thrill is gone. What makes the inheritance a support and not a duty is the readiness to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.comfort_west: Arcanum “The Magician” · J · The outer portrait A joins the centre E through the theme of will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. If the passage is free, the person moves from thought to action quickly; if the role argues with the inner state, they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. Bringing outer and inner into line takes a decision: pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.comfort_north: Arcanum “The Magician” · K · The talent on the line B–P–K takes shape as the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. A mature gift shows in moving from thought to action quickly; trying to earn recognition leads to dropping things halfway once the thrill is gone. The talent finds its shape when the person manages to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.comfort_east: Arcanum “The Magician” · L · The money line opens with the theme of will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. This is not a promise of income but a way in: at its best the person moves from thought to action quickly, out of balance they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. To turn the impulse into a steady business it helps to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.comfort_south: Arcanum “The Magician” · M · At the fork between relationships and the karmic tail this shows up: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. The first reaction helps closeness when the person moves from thought to action quickly, and sets off the old script when they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. Not walking in circles takes a pause in which you can pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.love_middle: Arcanum “The Magician” · R1 · The main question of the couple becomes initiative: who proposes, who decides, whose “let’s go” moves shared matters along. Nothing goes stale next to such a person: they are the first to invite, the first to make peace and the first to start something new. Initiative without agreement turns into one-man rule: the other one stops keeping up and quietly steps aside. Before every “let’s go” of your own, wait for an answer out loud rather than for silent consent.
in_positions.harmony: Arcanum “The Magician” · spiritual · The personal and the social levels are joined by the theme of will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. Agreement with yourself is felt when the person moves from thought to action quickly; the inner argument returns when they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. Tying the two levels into one direction takes the readiness to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.planetary: Arcanum “The Magician” · planetary · Beyond a personal biography goes the theme of will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. The contribution becomes visible to many when the person moves from thought to action quickly; the scale stays a pretty idea if they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. Starting from real influence and not from a loud role takes a decision: pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.purpose_personal: Arcanum “The Magician” · personal · With no audience the person would choose this theme: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. Being true to yourself shows in moving from thought to action quickly; walking away from your own task shows in dropping things halfway once the thrill is gone. This position comes alive when you manage to pick one thing and take it to the first result.
in_positions.purpose_social: Arcanum “The Magician” · social · Others can lean on this theme: the will and the skill to start first, without waiting for anyone’s permission. In shared work they are most useful when they move from thought to action quickly; the role stops working when they drop things halfway once the thrill is gone. Steady usefulness instead of an image comes from a concrete choice: pick one thing and take it to the first result.

items.repeat: A doubled start makes drive run through everything: where others are still choosing, this person has already begun — and begun in several matters at once. The danger is that launching becomes the answer to any task: one thing asks for a sprint, another for finishing what was started. Tell apart where a first step is needed and where the work has to be carried to the end, or a pile of bright beginnings gathers with not a single finish.

article.title: Arcanum 1 in the destiny matrix — The Magician: meaning, calling card and talents
article.short: 1 in the destiny matrix is The Magician, the arcanum of the first step. It is the energy that turns “I want to” into “I’m doing it”: an idea takes shape by your own hands, out of what is already there, without waiting for perfect conditions. It is one of the two rarest arcana in the matrix. Among its points, 1 turns up only for people born on the first of any month — then The Magician is the calling card — or in January, when he sits in the spiritual task and opens the line of talent. In the plus, The Magician is a master: he starts, strikes deals and carries an idea through to something that works. In the minus, he is a conjurer: he puts on a show instead of doing the work, or never quite lets himself begin.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 1: The Magician — who has it and what it means
seo.description: Destiny matrix 1 is The Magician, the arcanum of the first step. Only people born on the 1st or in January have it: what it means and where it’s sought in vain.

sections.h2: What 1 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: One is where counting starts, and the card means just that: the first move. In Waite’s deck [The Fool](/encyclopedia/arcanum/22) comes before The Magician as card zero; in the matrix he is number twenty-two and closes the circle. Benebell Wen, author of Holistic Tarot, tells them apart like this: with The Fool “it is still unclear which fork the fool will choose”, while The Magician “has chosen and is acting”. After The Magician comes [The High Priestess](/encyclopedia/arcanum/2) — knowledge that stays within. The Magician is the same knowledge brought out into the open and put to work.

The key thing to grasp about this card is that **The Magician does not create out of nothing.** Wen stresses that he is “someone who creates from what already exists”. You see this in life straight away. A person with a strong 1 does not wait for the money, the time, the diploma and the right team to turn up. They look at what they have today — two free evenings, an old laptop, a friend who knows the subject — and put a first version together from that. Rough, but alive. While others are still debating how it ought to be done, they already have something to show.

The Magician’s second side is the word. In Waite’s list of divinatory meanings the card opens with “skill, diplomacy, address, subtlety”, and only later comes “self-confidence, will”. Wen links The Magician to Mercury, which in astrology is the planet of speech, trade and messages. So 1 is not just drive. It is the knack of explaining an idea so that people start to help, of reaching agreement where others argue, and of selling an idea before it has become a thing. That last one is a strength and a risk at once.

The third side is focus. Wen calls The Magician “the card of individuality” and likens it to Newton’s first law of motion: “an object in motion will stay in motion until an external force is applied to stop it”. The power of 1 runs in a single direction; spread across ten projects, it vanishes. Waite says the same thing in loftier terms: “in a very high sense it is thought, in the fixation thereof”. A thought that has stopped being a dream and become a decision.

And one last thing, without which The Magician turns into a caricature. For Waite this is a card not of personal cleverness but of “the divine motive in man”, of “the possession and communication of the Powers and Gifts of the Spirit”. His Magician is not the source of power but its conductor: the power runs through him into the work. In everyday terms, 1 works best when a person serves the work rather than their own image. Once the work becomes a stage for a flashy act, the master turns into a conjurer.

sections.h2: Who has a 1 in their matrix
paragraphs: Arcanum 1 is the only one that addition cannot produce in the matrix. Almost every point of the chart is a sum of other points, and the sum of two arcana is never less than two. Numbers above 22 are reduced by adding their digits: 23 → 5, 30 → 3, 44 → 8. Such a reduction yields 1 only from 100, and a hundred is reached only in the totals of the chakra table, where seven numbers are added at once. That is why **the arcanum of beginnings stands only in the starting points** — the places where nothing has been added yet: the day and the month of birth.

paragraphs: Altogether, 13.8% of people have a 1 somewhere in their matrix — about one in seven. We counted this across all 46,300 dates from 1 January 1900 to October 2026. Only The High Priestess is rarer (13.4%), while each of the other twenty arcana turns up in the charts of 59–85% of people. So The Magician is no mark of the chosen and no “main card” — but it is not something everyone gets either.

In every other point nobody ever has a 1: not in the centre, not in the karmic tail, not in the money or relationship lines, not in the purposes, not in the family lines. Why people sometimes “find” it there is explained below, in the section on where people look for The Magician in vain. 1 as the arcanum of the year is calculated differently and has a page of its own: [1 for the year in the destiny matrix](/year/1).

One more clarification. A 1 in the matrix is the number of a card, not a numerological “life path number”. Numerology adds all the digits of a date into one, while the matrix keeps each point separate, and each has its own role. So reading a 1 always starts with the question of where it stands.

sections.h2: 1 as the calling card: born on the first of the month
paragraphs: The calling card is point A, the birth day arcanum. It shows not the whole personality but what people notice before anything else: your pace, the way you open a conversation, the role you are handed in a new group. For anyone born on the 1st, this point holds The Magician.

From the first meeting, people read this person as someone who knows where to start. While the group is still talking, they say, “Let me sketch a draft by tonight” — and by tonight the draft exists. They speak quickly and to the point, find words easily and explain complicated things in plain language. In a new team they are soon given the role of the starter: launch the project, run the first meeting, strike a deal with the person nobody else can get through to. **The Magician’s calling card sounds like a promise: with this person, things will get moving.**

That impression has a flip side: it travels faster than the person. People decide they will cope anyway and offer no help, even when help is needed. And anyone who sees the dexterity but not yet the result starts to suspect a trick: too smooth a talker, too quick to agree. Waite’s “subtlety” is easily read as cunning. The simplest way to check your calling card is by what repeats: what different people say about you when you first meet, and what they already expect of you by the second meeting.

The calling card also leads the first decade of life: on the age scale, point A covers the years from birth to ten. A childhood under The Magician often sounds like “I can do it myself!” The child takes toys apart to see how they work, bargains with adults, takes on things they have not yet grown into. A ban sounds to them like a dare. Real errands and real tools suited to their age work better: The Magician grows when what he does is of use to someone.

Next to the calling card, in the “Character” section, stands the card of the month, point B. It decides which card works in tandem with The Magician. This is also where a curious property of 1 shows: **added to any card except The Fool, it moves that card exactly one step forward.** The decade from 10 to 20 is the sum of the day and the month, so for people born on the 1st it is always led by the card one number higher than their birth month. The Magician replaces nothing — he takes the next step.

paragraphs: The same sum sits in the emotions of Sahasrara, the top chakra, which governs the link to a bigger plan. And for people born on the 1st, the physics of that chakra is The Magician himself. The row reads “1, the month, the month plus one”: for someone born on 1 March it is 1-3-4. For you, a bigger plan is something to be done, not dreamt about. There is more on the top chakra in the article on [Sahasrara](/encyclopedia/chakra/sahasrara).

sections.h2: 1 in the line of talent and the spiritual task: born in January
paragraphs: For people born in January, The Magician stands in point B, at the top of the chart. This is the spiritual task — a quality a person learns to handle from the inside. Its energy shows early and so is easily mistaken for an inborn gift. With 1 that is exactly what happens: the readiness to take things on yourself and to pick up new skills fast is noticed early, and it is easy to take it for a ready-made talent.

But a task is wider than an ability. Nimble hands and a silver tongue are not enough. The Magician’s task in point B is to become the author of your own actions: to start without waiting to be invited or allowed, to answer for what you set going, and to use your skill honestly — for the work, not for effect. The inner question of people born in January runs something like this: “Which of the things I’ve done are truly mine?” The same point opens the sky line, and in the section on tasks of the soul The Magician comes as the first task. For January births the total of the sky line always equals the karmic task plus one: here too, 1 moves the neighbouring card one step on.

When people ask about “1 in talents”, they mean exactly the January case. The line of talent B–P–K in the “Profession and work you love” section is read like this: the first card is the raw material, the second the method, the third the result. For people born in January the raw material of talent is The Magician: hands, words, initiative, the ability to master a new tool quickly. The other two cards are built the same way for everyone born in January, and this is one of the most elegant patterns in the matrix: **both come from the centre of the chart.** The result is the centre plus one, the method is the centre plus two (if that goes above 22, the digits are added). For example, for people born on 15 January 1990 the centre is 7, The Chariot, and the line of talent is 1-9-8: The Magician, The Hermit, Justice.

Our reading: the talent of January births does not come from outside. It is their own centre — the place where they feel at home and at ease — moved one step and two steps forward. The Magician adds no borrowed abilities; he carries further what is already in a person. That is exactly how Wen describes the card: creating from what already exists.

Where does this raw material earn money without burning a person out? Wherever the start depends on you and the work of your hands and head can be seen. Launching a new line of business, prototypes and pilots, a craft with tools — from joinery to code to cooking — sales and negotiation, teaching a skill in a “watch how it’s done” way, a practice of your own. A 1 has the hardest time where for years you must carry out someone else’s initiative and the result dissolves into a shared report. Then it is worth changing not the field but the form: an accountant with a 1 comes alive when asked to build a new accounting system rather than keep the old one running.

On the age scale point B leads the third decade, so for everyone born in January the years from 20 to 30 pass under The Magician. It is a decade of firsts that are your own: the first craft, the first job where the result depends on you, the first venture started without a prompt. The main question of these years is not “What should I be?” but “What can I do on my own that someone actually needs?” The risk lies in two extremes: trying everything and mastering nothing, or waiting until thirty for the perfect start.

In the chakra table the January Magician stands in the energy of Sahasrara: what drives you towards a bigger plan is the wish to make it real, not to contemplate it. In “Character” he is paired with the birth day arcanum: born on 15 January — read [The Magician and The Devil](/encyclopedia/combination/1-15); born on 31 January — 31 reduces to 4, and that is [The Magician and The Emperor](/encyclopedia/combination/1-4). For January births the decade from 10 to 20 is led by the day arcanum plus one: for those born on 15 January that is 16, The Tower.

sections.h2: 1 January: two Magicians in one chart
paragraphs: 1 January is the only date in the year when 1 stands in two points at once: the calling card and the spiritual task. Two Magicians do not mean twice the willpower: the points play different roles, and what is interesting is precisely that they coincide. **What people see in you from the first meeting is exactly what you have yet to learn.**

That is the trap. The outer Magician — confident, deft, ready to take things on — is so convincing that the inner work is easy to skip. Everyone around is sure you will manage, and you start believing it instead of testing it. The task for people born on 1 January is not to let the image outrun the work: the skill others see has to be proved again and again by what actually gets done.

Their age scale is curious too. Childhood passes under The Magician, the twenties under The Magician again, and between them, from 10 to 20, every one of them without exception has The High Priestess: 1 + 1 = 2. Our reading: two decades of action divided by a decade of quiet. The teenage years may be lived inwardly — in reading, in watching, in a closed world of one’s own — and when The Magician goes out to people the second time, he comes not empty-handed but with what The High Priestess has managed to gather. The same High Priestess sits in the emotions of Sahasrara: the top chakra row for people born on 1 January is 1-1-2. For you, action and the wish to act are one and the same, and you live it quietly, without an audience.

sections.h2: Master or conjurer: The Magician in the plus and in the minus
paragraphs: First, a common misconception. A number taken from a date of birth is never reversed, and “1 in the minus” is not a special card but the same energy used the wrong way. The Magician’s plus and minus are made of one material — dexterity. The question is what it works for. It is no accident that old decks called this card the Juggler, a street conjurer. **The master and the conjurer can do the same things; the difference is what remains after the show.**

You know The Magician in the plus by what he has made. He ships the first version while others are arguing about the right one. He learns with his hands: instead of reading a fifth book on swimming, he gets into the water with a coach. He builds a team out of acquaintances, a budget out of whatever there is, time out of lunch breaks. He explains things so that people join in of their own accord, and makes deals that no side regrets later. And he leaves things behind: software people use, a stool people sit on, a course people learn from.
The minus of 1 comes in three forms, and they are opposites of one another.

ul: **A show instead of the work.** The ability to impress starts to stand in for the result: the presentation is ready before the product, the promise sounds better than the work looks later. From there it is one step to manipulation. The Magician knows well which words work on people, and in the minus he moves people rather than the work.

**The Magician who never starts.** The opposite tilt, and just as common. The skill is there, the tools are there, but the person waits for permission: one more course, one more certificate, a little more preparation. In a reading, Wen takes The Magician reversed as “an external force that has been applied to stop that advancing movement”. Often that force is someone else’s voice in your own head: “Who are you to start?”

**Doing it all alone.** Competence turns into loneliness. Tasks are not handed over because “it’s quicker to do it myself”; help is not asked for because nobody offers it anyway. The work hits the ceiling of one person’s two hands.

paragraphs: How do you tell the master from the conjurer in yourself? **A trick works only while no one can see how it is done. A craft works even when you show how.** If you would feel awkward letting the other person see how you won their agreement, it was a trick.

sections.h2: What to do if you have a 1 in your matrix

ol: **Start with what you have today.** Not with a plan but with a first version: what can you make in one evening with the hands, money and people you already have? The Magician spends more strength waiting for the right conditions than on the work itself.

**Show what you’ve done, not what you’ve planned.** A 1 has a strong way with words, and that is the catch: an idea you have already talked about has had its share of admiration, and you feel less like doing it. Speak when you have something to show.
**Go deep into one craft.** The Magician grows as a master, and mastery is a tool learned so well that the hands know more than the head. Ten shallow skills make not a master but a conjurer.
**Test your methods for transparency.** Before an important conversation, ask yourself: would I be happy for the other person to see exactly how I am persuading them? If not, change the method.

**Hand over part of the work.** For a 1 this is not weakness but the move from a one-man act to a venture with more than two hands. A simple test: what would be left of your project if you went away for a month?

sections.h2: Where people look for The Magician in vain: the centre, tails, compatibility
paragraphs: **1 in the centre of the matrix.** The centre never holds a 1. The centre is the sum of the four main points of the chart, and, as we have seen, addition does not produce a 1. If some calculator has put a 1 in your centre — or in your calling card although you were born on the 23rd — it reduces large numbers by subtracting 22: 23 − 22 = 1. In the classic scheme this site uses, the digits are added: 23 → 2 + 3 = 5. Recalculate your date and read whichever card lands in the centre.

**The “Dark Magician”.** That is not 1. Popular readings use the name for the karmic tail 18-6-15 — The Moon, The Lovers and The Devil — and it has its own detailed page: [karmic tail 18-6-15](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/18-6-15). 1 never appears in the karmic tail, nor in the programs that repeat in circles. The same goes for the other “magical” names: “The Wizard” is [9-9-18](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-9-18), the “Magical Victim” is [9-18-9](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-18-9), love magic is [18-6-6](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/18-6-6). Every one of these tails contains The Moon, the card of mystery and reflected light, and not one contains The Magician. The magic of the popular programs is about spells and secrets; 1 is about craft.

**Compatibility.** In the compatibility matrix, where the matching points of two people are added together, 1 never comes up either: that is how Yuliana Lisovskaya calculates it, for example, in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility). If both partners have The Magician in the same point — both born on the 1st, or both in January — the compatibility matrix will show a 2 there, The High Priestess. For Lisovskaya, a 2 in these points describes a couple who keep a great deal to themselves and understand each other from half a word. Two Magicians together give not double the drive but quiet. And how The Magician gets on with other arcana within one personal matrix is covered on the combination pages — from [The Magician and The High Priestess](/encyclopedia/combination/1-2) to [The Magician and The Fool](/encyclopedia/combination/1-22).

sections.h2: Waite’s Magician: the gesture, the table and the sign of infinity
paragraphs: The best-known image of this card comes from the deck of Arthur Edward Waite, drawn by Pamela Colman Smith and published in 1909. In The Pictorial Key to the Tarot Waite describes “a youthful figure in the robe of a magician, having the countenance of divine Apollo, with smile of confidence and shining eyes”. He stands before a table, and almost every detail here means something.

**The gesture.** The right hand raises a wand towards heaven; the left points to the earth. According to Waite, this “dual sign is known in very high grades of the Instituted Mysteries” and shows “the descent of grace, virtue and light, drawn from things above and derived to things below”. Wen reads the gesture as the Hermetic formula “As Above, So Below”: “every plane of consciousness and every level of existence is interconnected”.

**The table.** On it lie the symbols of the four Tarot suits — wand, cup, sword and pentacle. Waite calls them “the elements of natural life, which lie like counters before the adept, and he adapts them as he wills”. This is where Wen draws the conclusion on which this whole article rests: The Magician creates from what already exists, not from nothing.

**The sign of infinity and the serpent.** Above the magician’s head is a figure 8 lying on its side — for Waite, “the mysterious sign of the Holy Spirit, the sign of life”. His belt is a serpent devouring its own tail. Usually that is a symbol of eternity, but here, Waite specifies, it means “the eternity of attainment in the spirit”.

**Roses and lilies.** Flowers grow below. Waite recognises in them a line from the Song of Songs, flos campi and lilium convallium, “the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys” — only here the wild flowers are “changed into garden flowers, to shew the culture of aspiration”. For 1 this may be the most precise image of all: an impulse is worth nothing until it has been cultivated, like a garden.

**The Juggler.** Waite knew the card had another face. In older decks the first trump showed a conjurer — in the French, Marseille tradition he is Le Bateleur, a fairground trickster. Waite lists him as “the Magus, Magician, or Juggler, the caster of the dice and mountebank, in the world of vulgar trickery” and dismisses this as “the colportage interpretation”, a pedlar’s reading far from the true meaning of the symbol. In the same passage he quotes Éliphas Lévi: the Magus signifies “that unity which is the mother of numbers”. The one from which all counting begins.

In readings, Waite made this card stand for “the Querent, if male”. That has nothing to do with the matrix: gender does not change a single number in the calculation, and for women a 1 reads exactly the same. Nor is there a reversed position in the matrix — instead, people speak of the energy in the plus and in the minus.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: Meaning of the card: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (text of the 1922 reissue), and Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015). Both are quoted in their original English.
Compatibility: Yuliana Lisovskaya, Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024).

Calculation: the classic destiny matrix scheme, with numbers reduced by adding their digits, as in this site’s calculator. All shares and patterns were checked by running through 46,300 dates from 1 January 1900 to 6 October 2026.

The reading of the positions, the rule that 1 moves a card one step forward, the January line of talent and the age scale of 1 January are our interpretation based on these sources. This is a symbolic reading, not a forecast of events.

items.title: The High Priestess
items.short: instinct ahead of arguments: reads the situation before anyone explains it
meaning: The second arcanum in the destiny matrix is the energy of perception: not of action, but of taking in. If the first arcanum does things and announces itself, the second first reads the situation and only then decides whether it is worth showing up at all. The High Priestess is about knowledge that comes before any proof, and about the pause between the impulse and the deed, where understanding is born.

In character this is a quiet, receiving force — not pressure but sensitivity. The two thinks not in results but in pictures: out of pauses, tones of voice and small details it puts the whole together faster than it manages to justify it. From the inside it feels like “I just know” — the conclusion is ready, and the explanation for it is built on afterwards. In noise and bustle such a person goes deaf; in silence they hear.

The main engine of the two is the need to understand before taking part, and its conflict is hidden right there. Knowledge for it is a value to be guarded, not spent: it feels far too well how easily openness gets turned into vulnerability. So the energy of the number is balancing all the time on the edge of being closed — the same depth that gives protection is also able to lock a person inside themselves.

The strength of the two is defined by where its knowledge is aimed. In the mature form it turns what it perceives into work and shares it, and people come to it for understanding where everyone else is rushing to conclusions. In the weak one it stores up what it has seen: the picture of the world is assembled, but there is no taking part in that picture, and from the outside such closedness reads as coldness. The difference is not in the sharpness of the sensitivity, but in whether the knowledge goes out or stays a load nobody has asked for.

Within the deck the two differs from its neighbours by the direction of the energy. The first arcanum, The Magician, is active and turned outwards — it begins and creates movement; the two is turned inwards — it takes in and waits for its moment. The third, The Empress, takes the same inner knowledge and generously carries it out into the world, grows and feeds; at this step the two still keeps everything to itself. Its place in the row is the pause of attention between someone else’s action and one’s own answer: understand first, then show up.

in_positions.character: Inside there is an observer. This person listens first and speaks later, so on first meeting they look closed. In fact they have already gathered three times more about you than you have about them.
in_positions.comfort: Calm comes in silence and alone, and this is not a whim: without an hour away from people, the instinct fades first. A noisy home and an open-plan office wear such a centre out faster than any workload.
in_positions.profession: The gift is a feel for people and for subtext. It works in psychology, analysis and expert review, wherever the unsaid has to be understood. Staying out of the spotlight is no obstacle — this talent is paid for without publicity; the real obstacle is a guess that has replaced checking the facts. Their true work begins where fine observation gets a clear form: a conclusion, a recommendation or a decision that holds up when it is tested.
in_positions.realisation: This line leads to depth, not to volume. Their business is to become the person others come to for understanding, and that happens by itself if they do not force themselves to be loud and self-promoting.
in_positions.karma40: For arcanum two the lens of age picks out the question of voice. Silence feels safe, so the important thing stays unsaid and is later decided for them by someone else. One clear no, said in time, changes the story faster than five years of patience.
in_positions.resources: Good things come in through knowledge and through people who trust them. Not advertising but a recommendation; not a stream but the right person at the right moment. The condition is not to hide what you can do until you feel completely sure.
in_positions.family_gifts: The family line passed down a fine ear and the ability to keep things. There was a woman who knew everything about everyone and said nothing: people came to her with what they could not say aloud. That gift still holds them up today — in negotiations and in hard conversations, where hearing matters more than answering.
in_positions.soul_tasks: Trusting their own signals is the work of the soul here. Half the trouble of this arcanum is that they saw it all in advance, kept quiet and then blamed themselves. Telling instinct apart from anxiety has to be learned from their own notes.
in_positions.past_lives: In the tail lies the habit of expecting to be understood without words. The instinct is real: they pick up a mood before anyone names it. The request is never spoken aloud, resentment over what was not guessed piles up, and from the outside it looks like coldness for no reason. Once a week, name one of your own wishes directly, without testing whether anyone will guess it.
in_positions.purpose: Purpose here is to be the one who sees and translates: between people, and between a person and their own state. No stage and no microphone are needed, only one conversation after which the other person finally sees clearly.
in_positions.money: What is paid for is access to knowledge: consultations, readings, expert opinion, analysis. The money comes in more quietly than for the neighbours, but without the race. The brake is shyness — waiting in silence to be valued. Name the sum first, before the client asks about it: silence costs more here than awkwardness.
in_positions.money40: By arcanum two, years of practice make the same observations noticeably dearer: behind the instinct now stand hundreds of other people’s cases. The best move is out of doing the work and into being called in to look at a situation and say what is really going on. One thing holds it back — the habit of keeping quiet until asked: an unspoken observation does not get paid for. Take one case from practice and sell the reading separately from the work itself.
in_positions.relations: In a relationship they give depth and patience, but they need room. People near them get used to pauses and to answers that do not come at once. Pressure on such a person shuts them down for a month. One direct question works better here than a month of guessing, but the answer has to be waited for in silence.
in_positions.parents_children: Understanding without words is the family rule of this arcanum: the mood of the house was read from the steps in the hallway, and nothing was named aloud. The same way carries on — they feel the state of a younger one before that one dares to say it. There is a single danger: silent closeness easily turns into a home where everyone guesses and nobody talks anything through.
in_positions.ancestry: The family line needs someone to finally say it aloud. Family secrets, unnamed stories, we-do-not-talk-about-that — the task is to stop guarding them and give the events their names back. Write down one story the family only hinted at, separating known facts from guesses and other people’s versions.
in_positions.body_resource: Her strength lasts as long as the quiet does: water, a walk alone and an evening without other voices bring it back. In a good state she goes into silence early, before she starts snapping at the people close to her, and comes back to them on her own. The first sign that the reserve is running low is irritation at people she usually puts up with easily, while solitude that drags on quietly turns into a way of not deciding. Notice after how many hours of quiet the clarity returns, and stop there.
in_positions.chakras: High Priestess: the level works through the theme of knowledge that comes not from reasoning but from silence. The strong move is to see the unspoken and to understand before the explanation; the failure looks like a closedness that even the nearest people cannot reach. One thing brings the footing back: check a hunch with words, not only with an inner feeling.
in_positions.rest: Solitude with content restores them: a book, water, a forest, a museum with no guide. A noisy break in company does the opposite — they come back emptier than they left. The easiest way to tell the break worked is the quiet in their head: fewer thoughts, and finally their own.
in_positions.loops: The circle goes like this: they noticed, they kept quiet, they waited for the trouble, they took offence. Until the signal is spoken aloud at the moment it appears, the story repeats with new people and in the same shapes.
in_positions.years: A decade of the High Priestess is rarely loud: study, watching, getting strength back, a deliberate step into the shade. What was gathered in silence goes to work if the watching turns into a decision: a direction chosen, conditions named, a no said aloud. The stage is slowed by the habit of waiting for complete certainty: while clarity is thin, a person keeps quiet for years and misses their turn. Name in advance the sign by which the watching counts as finished and it is time to speak.
