paragraphs: A 5 also turns up in the reading by decades — for 48% of people. The age scale runs along the outer points of the chart: the personality portrait governs the first ten years of life, the spiritual task the years from 20 to 30, the material task from 40 to 50, the karmic task from 60 to 70, and the family points the stretches in between. Such a decade most often passes under the sign of apprenticeship, your own or someone else’s: the person looks for a mentor, truly masters a trade or takes on pupils for the first time.

sections.h2: The karmic tail and the program of the 5
paragraphs: The karmic tail is the three lower numbers of the chart, running down from the centre: the entry, the middle and the karmic task. In the destiny matrix it is read as a storyline a person has brought with them and easily repeats until they notice it. One person in five has a 5 in the tail — 21.1% — and there are only three variants. A 5 never appears at the entry of the tail, so here it is either the middle or the root.

When the 5 is at the root, in the place of the karmic task, it is the lesson itself: to build your own relationship with rules and authority. When it is in the middle, the 5 is the mechanism, the thing that keeps the old circle turning: a rule, a rank or a vow that long ago became a chain.

ul: **[15-20-5](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-20-5)** — the most common of all 26 possible tails, found in 10.1% of people. The 5 is at the root. Popular readings call it the “Rebel”: a pull stronger than any rule (The Devil, 15) and an instant protest at someone else’s “that’s not how it’s done” (Judgement, 20). The task of the 5 here is neither to wage war on other people’s rules nor to give in to them, but to find a rule you would sign up to yourself.

**[15-5-8](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-5-8)** — 9.2% of people. The 5 is in the middle, between The Devil and Justice (8). Popular readings call it “Betrayal in the Family”: an oath or a family law turns into shackles over time, and then comes judgement, someone else’s or your own.

**[6-5-17](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-5-17)** — 1.8% of people. The 5 is in the middle, between The Lovers (6) and The Star (17). Popular readings call it “Pride”: a person starts living by other people’s ratings, and every talent becomes a rung on a ladder of rank. The task is to give your light without waiting for applause.

paragraphs: In two tails out of three the 5 sits next to The Devil, and for a reading that is a very telling neighbour. The Hierophant is a bond a person accepts of their own free will: a teaching, a vow, a rule. The Devil is a bond that holds them against their will: craving, fear, dependence. Tails with this pair show how one quietly turns into the other — and how to turn it back.

paragraphs.h3: The program of the 5: what goes round in circles

paragraphs: When people search for “program 5”, they usually mean a 5 in the points that make up a program — the karmic task or the centre of the chart (how programs work is explained [on a separate page](/programs)). A program is a storyline that repeats itself, with different people and in different settings. The 5 has four such storylines, and each one is recognised by its ending.

**The uninvited teacher.** You see how it ought to be done, and you explain. Nobody listens. You step back with a bitter “I told you so” — and next time you explain even harder. At a family dinner your brother hears not advice about his business but yet another lecture, and next time he simply won’t tell you what is going on. The way out is to answer the question you were asked, not the one you think they should have asked.

**The eternal student.** One more course, one more book, one more mentor — while your own business, your own consulting, your own writing keep being put off because “it’s too early”. Whatever the question, the person answers in someone else’s words. The way out is to release one thing into the world, imperfect as it may be, and sign it with your own name.

**The proper way.** Life runs by someone else’s rulebook: a profession the parents approved of, a marriage because “it’s time”, rules nobody ever checked. The person tries hard to do everything right and waits for it to be noticed and appreciated — and it isn’t. The way out is to test every rule with the question “why?” and keep the ones that have a living answer.

**The kindly secret.** The truth is held back to protect someone — and it surfaces at the worst possible moment, along with resentment at the silence. The way out is to tell the truth carefully and in measured doses, but to tell it.
Neither the tail nor the program is a sentence or a debt you have to “work off”. It is a habitual move that kicks in before you have time to choose. Notice it, and the choice is already there.

sections.h2: The 5 in love and marriage
paragraphs: The 5 is the arcanum of a union sealed by a word, and it brings seriousness to a relationship. It matters to a 5 that the couple share values and have things to talk about: the union rests not on household routine alone but on a shared sense of how to live and what for. A 5 likes a relationship to be named and made official, and a family to have its own holidays and its own way of life.

The difficulties grow out of that same seriousness. One partner gradually takes the mentor’s chair, and every argument becomes an exam the other has failed in advance. Other people’s rulebooks move into the home: “in my family we did it this way”, “Mum thinks otherwise”. For more on how the arcanum sounds in a couple, see [5 in relationships](/encyclopedia/position/relations/5) and [5 under the heart](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/5).

sections.h2: Money, work and calling
paragraphs: At work a 5 is strongest where something complicated has to be made clear, or where rules and standards come first: mentoring and teaching, staff training and course design, law, editing and translation, guided tours and popular science, archives, museums and libraries, service in a religious community, certification and quality control, sports refereeing. In any profession a 5 sooner or later becomes the one who shows newcomers the ropes. And it usually earns not from a product but from what it knows and can explain.

The typical trap is endless preparation: “once I finish one more course, I’ll start charging”. The knowledge piles up, while people who know just as much get paid because they dared to go out to people sooner. More in [5 on the money line](/encyclopedia/position/money/5) (the question about a “5 under the dollar sign” belongs there too: that is what people call a 5 in the middle of the money line, point R2) and in [the talent of the 5](/encyclopedia/position/profession/5).

sections.h2: The 5 for women and for men
paragraphs: Gender plays no part in the calculation: the matrix adds up only the day, month and year of birth, and a man and a woman born on the same day have exactly the same numbers. The meaning of the arcanum does not change with gender either.

What changes is something else: which ready-made rules the people around you offer. And ready-made rules are The Hierophant’s very subject. So the questions “how a woman ought to behave” and “what a real man should be” are not background for a 5 but its direct work: to accept these rules as your own, to rewrite them or to turn them down — but consciously, not because that is how your parents did it.

A woman with a strong 5 may keep the family’s way of life, or she may found a school of her own — and the second is every bit as much a 5 as the first. A man with a 5 may become a mentor, a man of faith, the elder of his family — or an interpreter of complex ideas for thousands of people. The arcanum sets the theme, passing on knowledge and your stance towards rules, not a role you have to play.

sections.h2: The 5 in compatibility
paragraphs: Here it is important to tell two cases apart.

**A 5 in the partners’ personal charts.** If one or both of them have it, values and rules — “the way we do things” — are a strong theme in the couple. Common ground comes quickly when their views coincide, and hard when each has brought their own rulebook into the home. Two fives under one roof would do well to agree in advance which things one of them teaches and which the other.

**A 5 in the couple’s matrix.** This matrix is calculated separately: the matching points of the two personal charts are added together and reduced to a number from 1 to 22. The calculation is set out step by step in Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book “Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost” (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility), and there the couple’s points mean something different from the points of a personal chart. A 5 in the couple’s matrix describes a union of the traditional kind: the couple have their own rules and stick to them; the partners are friends as well, with shared views and plenty to talk about; authority in the family is accepted willingly, and money is handled carefully and jointly. The flip side is the urge to remake each other, lecturing, intolerance of other opinions, and relatives who get too far into the couple’s life. The author’s advice to such couples is to get on with the relatives but not to let them inside their boundaries, and to start holidays and traditions of their own rather than only inheriting other people’s.
The matrix gives no compatibility percentage. A 5 in a couple is not a score for the union but a description of what holds it together and what it may trip over.

sections.h2: A Hierophant year
paragraphs: A year under the 5 is a time to lean on what others have already tested: to go and study, to find a mentor, to put agreements in writing. What it brings and where it gets stuck is covered in [arcanum 5 for the year](/year/5).

sections.h2: The Hierophant and its neighbours
paragraphs: The 5 is easier to understand once you set it beside the cards it resembles.

ul: **The High Priestess (2).** Both cards are about knowledge, but The High Priestess knows silently and from within, while The Hierophant teaches out loud. Waite draws the line in exactly this way: he is “the ruling power of external religion, as the High Priestess is the prevailing genius of the esoteric, withdrawn power”. [The High Priestess and The Hierophant](/encyclopedia/combination/2-5).

**The Emperor (4).** Both stand for power, but of different kinds. The Emperor rules what can be built and defended, The Hierophant what people believe in and consider right. Wen puts it like this: “If The Emperor is about having authority from government or the Father, then The Hierophant is about having authority from the Divine.” [The Emperor and The Hierophant](/encyclopedia/combination/4-5).

**The Lovers (6).** The Hierophant joins people by rule and vow, The Lovers by feeling and choice. A union needs both; in the 6-5-17 tail these cards stand side by side. [The Hierophant and The Lovers](/encyclopedia/combination/5-6).

**The Hermit (9).** Also a teacher, but a different one. The Hierophant teaches many — to a syllabus, in a school, within a tradition. The Hermit seeks along his own path and shares what he finds with whoever comes to him of their own accord. [The Hierophant and The Hermit](/encyclopedia/combination/5-9).
**The Devil (15).** The shadow of the 5: a bond that holds you against your will. [The Hierophant and The Devil](/encyclopedia/combination/5-15).

sections.h2: Waite’s Hierophant: what the classic card shows
paragraphs: In the Waite–Smith deck (1909) The Hierophant wears a triple crown and sits between two pillars. Waite points out at once that “they are not those of the Temple which is guarded by the High Priestess”: hers is the way into the hidden, his is the open, outer side of the teaching. In his left hand The Hierophant holds “a sceptre terminating in the triple cross”. His right hand is raised in “the well-known ecclesiastical sign which is called that of esotericism, distinguishing between the manifest and concealed part of doctrine”. And Waite adds: “It is noticeable in this connexion that the High Priestess makes no sign.”

At The Hierophant’s feet lie crossed keys, and two ministers kneel before him; Benebell Wen notes that one is “cloaked in red roses and another in white lilies”. The keys stand for “the power of the keys”: in Christian tradition the keys promised to the apostle Peter mean the right to “bind and loose” — to decide what is allowed and what is not. Waite approves of the formula given by Grand Orient, who “says truly that the Hierophant is the power of the keys, exoteric orthodox doctrine, and the outer side of the life which leads to the doctrine”. The amusing part is that Grand Orient, whom Waite praises for accuracy, is Waite himself: it is the pen name under which he had earlier published a book on fortune-telling with cards.

Then comes the heart of it. Waite’s Hierophant is “the summa totius theologiæ, when it has passed into the utmost rigidity of expression”, and at the same time he symbolises “all things that are righteous and sacred on the manifest side”. He is “the channel of grace belonging to the world of institution as distinct from that of Nature”; he is “the order and the head of the recognized hierarchy, which is the reflection of another and greater hierarchic order”. He is not philosophy, he is not inspiration, and he is not religion itself, “although he is a mode of its expression”. Hence the warning about the pontiff who forgets that he is only a sign.

Lay The Devil (15) from the same deck beside him and you will see a rhyme: again a figure raised up high and two people below, only instead of ministers there are chained captives. A vow and a chain are built alike; the difference is whether a person is held by choice or by fear.

paragraphs.h3: The fifth arcanum in a tarot reading

paragraphs: In Waite’s list of divinatory meanings the upright Hierophant is “Marriage, alliance, captivity, servitude; by another account, mercy and goodness; inspiration; the man to whom the Querent has recourse”. Reversed: “Society, good understanding, concord, over-kindness, weakness.” Benebell Wen reads the card in a modern key: upright, “conforming to what is the present norm, membership in the majority, and having the approval of those in power”; reversed, nonconformity, your own path in defiance of the rules — and for her that is, if anything, a good sign: “The Hierophant in reverse is considered a good omen card.”

In the destiny matrix a card is never reversed: the calculated number simply stands in its point. The plus and the minus of the 5 are two ways of living one and the same energy, not the position of a card in a spread.

sections.h2: Pope, Priest, Teacher: why the card has so many names
paragraphs: In the Italian decks of the Renaissance and in the French Tarot de Marseille the fifth arcanum is simply the Pope. Waite lists other names too — the High Priest, the Spiritual Father, even the Abbot — and remarks: “I think, however, that in its primitive form this card did not represent the Roman Pontiff.” In the eighteenth century, in the so-called Besançon tarot, the Pope and the Popess were replaced altogether by Jupiter and Juno: the seat of highest authority remained, and only the figure on it changed.

It was the Frenchman Antoine Court de Gébelin who tied the fifth arcanum to hierophants, in 1781: he believed the tarot was a legacy of Egyptian priests and looked for traces of the ancient mysteries in its cards. More than a century later, in the English Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, to which Waite belonged, the hierophant was the officer who led the initiation rite, and the Waite–Smith deck fixed the name. It is more precise than “Pope”: the point is not a particular church but anyone who brings a person into a circle of knowledge. The word “pontiff” has a lovely inner form as well: Latin pontifex is built from the words for “bridge” and “to make”. Historians still argue about where the title really came from, but the image of a bridge suits the fifth arcanum perfectly.

In Russian-language destiny matrix readings the names that took hold are the Priest and the Teacher. The Teacher is the most practical of them: it tells you straight away what this energy is busy with in life.

sections.h2: How to live the 5 in the plus

ol: **Ask before you teach.** “Do you want advice, or do you just want me here?” — one question like that, and the conversation stops being a lesson.
**Keep the chain alive at both ends.** Find someone to learn from right now — a living person, not only books. And someone to teach: pass one of your skills on to one person.
**Test rules with “why?”.** If the only answer to why something is done is “that’s the custom”, the rule has to be either filled with meaning or let go.
**Speak in the first person.** Instead of “it is generally held” and “according to so-and-so’s method” — “I think” and “I have checked”.
**Welcome disagreement.** A good teacher is glad of a pupil who goes further. The best test is whether people can argue with you and stay on good terms.

**Review your vows.** Once a year, ask yourself about your main commitments: would I choose this again? If yes, it is a union. If I hold on only because “I have to”, it is time for an honest conversation.
**Don’t keep the truth back “for their own good”.** Before you stay silent, ask yourself: in their place, would I want to know?
**Start a tradition of your own.** Don’t only inherit a way of life — create one: a small ritual, a holiday, a rule that keeps your people together.

paragraphs: A good hierophant is known not by how much they know but by how many people around them have learned to understand things for themselves.

items.title: The Lovers
items.short: attraction and choice: draws people close and demands you decide who exactly
meaning: Six in the destiny matrix is the arcanum of The Lovers, the energy of attraction and union. The simplest way to describe it is with one sign: the six is the “and” between people, the point where two of them find each other. This person’s strength switches on not alone but in a pair — one plus one gives them not two, but noticeably more.

To be a six means living on response. The main driver here is neither will nor an idea but resonance: the energy lights up when someone answers — a glance, a liking, a “yes” coming back. Hence the steady inner hum of “is this my person, is this my place”, which sounds quietly even in calm years. Such a person measures life less by what they have done than by whom they did it with and who stood beside them.

Sewn into this energy is one eternal question — choice, because a union always comes down to “with whom exactly”. This is where the arcanum’s main test lies. The strong version is the one who can make up their mind and then stand by it: they become a bridge, they join people who do not work together apart, and they hold that tie for years. The weak version gets stuck in an endless “maybe”: it stays open to everyone at once, just to be liked, and so it truly belongs to no one.

It is easy to mistake the six for plain sociability. The point is not that the person likes people, but that their fate runs through someone else: growth, turning points, the very feeling of “I am in my place” are born not inside but at the joint with another. That is why both the joy and the main mistakes of this arcanum always have somebody’s face; they do not appear in silence, alone with oneself.

Neighbouring arcana help you feel the six by contrast. The seventh, The Chariot, goes out into the world on its own — by its own will, towards its own victory, asking nobody. The same road taken solo is hard for the six: without a companion the movement loses its sense, because its strength is not in arriving first but in arriving together.

in_positions.character: The first thing people notice is how easy this person is to talk to. They are liked quickly, a conversation with them runs by itself, and in almost any company they turn out to be one of their own. Behind that hides a constant doubt whenever something has to be chosen.
in_positions.comfort: Things feel good where somebody else is nearby: a shared project, a partner, a talk that runs late into the night. Such a centre takes solitude badly, and when solitude is forced on it, it feels like punishment and the search for any company at all begins.
in_positions.profession: A talent for connecting people and finding a common language. It works in negotiation, in recruiting, in sales, in anything done in pairs or through a go-between. Solitary work in silence costs this gift half its strength. It is best tested on a task where two sides start out speaking different languages and finish with one agreed decision.
in_positions.realisation: The road runs through partnership. Solo projects wither for such a person, while with the right person beside them three times as much gets done. The main work of a lifetime is to choose that person deliberately, and not by the sympathy of the first week.
in_positions.karma40: In the first grown-up forks of the road the sixth arcanum tests choice and responsibility. While the decision is put off, the situation drains strength out of both options. The story changes after the first honest yes to one and no to the other.
in_positions.resources: Resource comes in through people: an introduction, a recommendation, a partner who opens a door. The condition is simple, do not hide. The channel narrows in exactly those months when the person has stopped talking to anyone and sits alone.
in_positions.family_gifts: Charm and the knack of coming to terms arrived by inheritance. There was someone who settled matters through people rather than through force, and doors opened where others were battering at them. The ability still works, but it lives only in connections that are kept up: a contact nobody has called for years stops being an inheritance.
in_positions.soul_tasks: The work of the soul here is about staying true to yourself inside closeness. This arcanum dissolves easily into another person and a year later cannot remember what it wanted itself. The check is simple: does the person still have plans of their own, and not only shared ones?
in_positions.past_lives: From the past comes the habit of not choosing. The sensitivity to people here is rare: the person sees what another one lives by and gets close with ease. Doors are kept ajar until circumstances decide instead, and circumstances usually decide against them. Set a deadline for one postponed choice and say the decision out loud before that deadline runs out.
in_positions.purpose: The point of this road is to bring people together: to join what does not work separately, and to help others come to an agreement. Work like that almost always looks like working with couples and with teams.
in_positions.money: Money arrives here through people and connections: partnership, commission, sales, a shared business. A solo scheme brings in less. The hole is usually in boundaries, because it feels awkward to talk about money with people you like. Before a joint venture starts, write down who puts in how much, who takes out how much, and on what terms each side can walk away.
in_positions.money40: After forty the Six leans on the circle it has gathered: old clients, partnerships, a reputation as someone easy to deal with. Former connections bring in more than new acquaintances, because over the years it is already clear who pays and who comes back. The circle stops feeding the moment choosing is avoided: a scattered ‘nice to everybody’ turns it into a list of people you feel awkward quoting a price to. Pick five people out of that circle and offer each of them a specific piece of work for a specific sum.
in_positions.relations: Relationships are the central theme of this life, and the person gives a lot of warmth and attention inside them. The risk is well known: falling in love with being in love, and swinging between two people until both are tired of waiting for an answer. A choice postponed out of pity for both turns out in the end to be a decision somebody else made.
in_positions.parents_children: In this family the elders shared their worries as with an equal, and the difference in age wore off early. Friendship with a younger person starts easily for the same reason: they become a confidant before they are ready for it, whether that is a child, a student or a younger sister. It helps to keep the line of age rather than look in a younger person for a companion in worries.
in_positions.ancestry: Along the family line runs an inability to come to terms. People parted for good and did not speak for decades; the lesson here is to stay in contact. After the next quarrel, be the one who comes back first, if that is safe: one restored conversation is enough for the rule to stop being the only one.
in_positions.body_resource: Strength for the Lovers comes from people and from joy, and it is lost in conflict. One warm evening brings back almost the whole reserve, so the one who calls for a talk first, before resentment turns into a habit, holds up better. A long quarrel knocks you down harder than a day of heavy physical work, and agreeing for the sake of peace is the most expensive way to save a relationship. Say what is irritating you on the same day rather than a week later, and compare how much strength is left by the evening.
in_positions.chakras: The Lovers: what this level holds is attraction and choice. In resource it shows as joining people up and seeing who suits whom; in overload it shows as indecision dressed up as a wish to keep everything. To even it out, it helps to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.rest: Shared things restore this person: a trip with someone close, a long table with friends, dancing, any joy that takes two. Complete solitude turns rest into sitting it out with a phone in hand and no rest at all. It is not about the amount of entertainment: one close person present settles the question entirely.
in_positions.loops: The loop is recognised at once: two options, I play for time, I lose both. It repeats until the person learns to choose earlier than the moment when the choice gets made for them.
in_positions.years: The decade of the Lovers is a long fork in the road: partnership, important introductions, alliances where the price of every yes and no is visible straight away. The fork is passed like an adult if the person keeps their own position inside the agreement and does not buy consent at the cost of themselves. Putting off an answer so as to upset nobody costs more here than a straight refusal, and that is how both are lost. Name out loud the one condition without which the union does not work, and watch how it is taken.
in_positions.day: Arcanum “The Lovers” · A · The first impression is built around one theme: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. At full strength the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; under strain they drag a decision out to the last moment. The image turns into a steady reputation when they manage to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.month: Arcanum “The Lovers” · B · An inborn spiritual task switches itself on: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. So the person may not count it as a gift that they get close to people easily and build alliances; the other side shows when they drag a decision out to the last moment. The mature task of this position is to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.year: Arcanum “The Lovers” · C · The material task takes the theme of attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who, from intention into result. The strong side is visible in deeds: the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; when it tilts, they drag a decision out to the last moment. This position is lived out not by a promise but by a readiness to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.mission: Arcanum “The Lovers” · D · There is no punishment here, only a story that keeps coming back: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. The grown-up answer begins where the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances, while the old loop begins with the opposite: they drag a decision out to the last moment. Breaking the repeat takes a concrete decision, to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.center: Arcanum “The Lovers” · E · Choice stands at the centre of the chart: the person feels like themselves next to other people, and almost everything that matters to them is settled through relationships. They reach out to people sincerely, can choose with the heart and hold to what they chose without looking back. Support is lost by the one who weighs things endlessly, and while they have not decided, circumstances and somebody else’s insistence decide for them. Put a deadline on a disputed choice and name the decision out loud, even if it turns out to be inconvenient.
in_positions.father_line: Arcanum “The Lovers” · F · The spiritual male line keeps a principle: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. The strong side of the inheritance shows like this: the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; the heavy side of the script is dragging a decision out to the last moment. Taking the strength of the line without its rigidity means choosing before time makes the choice.
in_positions.mother_line: Arcanum “The Lovers” · G · The spiritual female line keeps the rule of the house: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. In the supporting version the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; in the tangled one they repeat something else, dragging a decision out to the last moment. Rewriting the rule while keeping its value takes one step: to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.descendants: Arcanum “The Lovers” · H · Here the family principle becomes an action: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. In its reliable form the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; the automatic form drags a decision out to the last moment. A new continuation of the male line starts with the ability to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.inheritance: Arcanum “The Lovers” · I · Here the values of the family line enter everyday life: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. The resource shows when the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; the usual tilt is dragging a decision out to the last moment. Making the inheritance a support rather than a duty takes a readiness to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.comfort_west: Arcanum “The Lovers” · J · The outer portrait A joins the centre E through the theme of attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. If the passage is free, the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; if the role argues with the inner state, they drag a decision out to the last moment. Bringing the outside and the inside together takes one decision: to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.comfort_north: Arcanum “The Lovers” · K · The talent on the B–P–K line takes its form from attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. A mature gift is noticeable because the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; an attempt to earn recognition leads to dragging a decision out to the last moment. The talent takes form when it becomes possible to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.comfort_east: Arcanum “The Lovers” · L · The money line opens with the theme of attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. This is not a promise of income but a way in: at its best the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances, and when it tilts they drag a decision out to the last moment. To turn the impulse into steady work, it helps to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.comfort_south: Arcanum “The Lovers” · M · At the fork of relationships and the karmic tail one thing shows up: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. The first reaction helps closeness when the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances, and it starts the old script when they drag a decision out to the last moment. Staying off the loop takes a pause in which it is possible to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.love_middle: Arcanum “The Lovers” · R1 · Relationships run into choice, and it comes round more often than anyone would like: between people, between the past and the present, between what is comfortable and what is alive. When the person chooses with the heart and does not look back, the couple gets a rare honesty. Endless weighing leaves both of them hanging, and in the end the decision is made by anyone at all except them. Set yourself a deadline and name the choice to your partner before it runs out, even if the decision turns out to be inconvenient.
in_positions.harmony: Arcanum “The Lovers” · spiritual · The personal and the social levels are joined by the theme of attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. Agreement with yourself is felt when the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; the inner argument comes back when they drag a decision out to the last moment. Tying the two levels into one direction takes a readiness to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.planetary: Arcanum “The Lovers” · planetary · Beyond a personal biography goes the theme of attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. The contribution becomes visible to many when the person gets close to people easily and builds alliances; the scale stays a nice idea if they drag a decision out to the last moment. Starting from real influence rather than a loud role takes one decision: to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.purpose_personal: Arcanum “The Lovers” · personal · With no audience at all the person would pick this theme: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. Being true to themselves shows in getting close to people easily and building alliances; walking away from their own task shows in dragging a decision out to the last moment. This position comes alive when it becomes possible to choose before time makes the choice.
in_positions.purpose_social: Arcanum “The Lovers” · social · Other people can lean on this theme: attraction and choice, a pull towards people and a demand to decide exactly who. In shared work the person is especially useful when they get close to people easily and build alliances; the role stops working when they drag a decision out to the last moment. Steady usefulness instead of an image comes from one concrete choice: to choose before time makes the choice.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 6 — The Lovers: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: 6 in the destiny matrix is the arcanum of The Lovers: attraction, union and choice. What the six means as a number, its strong and weak sides.

article.title: Arcanum 6 in the destiny matrix: The Lovers — love that chooses
article.short: In the destiny matrix, 6 is The Lovers, the energy of love, attraction and choice. Its main idea is a single one: to love is to choose. A person with a strong 6 is easy to like, has a fine feel for people and for beauty, and can bring together those who could not come to terms on their own. Their lesson is to do the choosing themselves: not to keep two options open, not to wait for someone else’s approval and not to trade a living person for a perfect picture. It is the most widespread arcanum in the matrix: 85% of people have a 6 in at least one position of their reading.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 6: The Lovers — meaning, program and karmic tail
seo.description: Destiny matrix 6 is The Lovers: to love is to choose. Why its minus turns cynical, where a 6 sits in your date, program 6, eight tails and couples.

sections.h2: What 6 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: In the destiny matrix the 6 is described with two words, love and choice, and they are often presented as two separate meanings. In fact they are one. You can fall for several people at once, for a voice, for an image, for a lucky coincidence — falling in love simply happens. Love begins later: at the moment when, out of many, you choose one — a person, a cause, a city — and go on choosing it when others turn up nearby. The energy of 6 is the passage from “I’m drawn to” to “I choose”, and on to “we’re together”.

So the arcanum has three layers. **Attraction** — a pull towards people and towards beauty: a phrase put just right, a happy combination of colours, a person who lights up when talking about the thing they love. **Choice** — a decision made with the heart, from your own values, not from a table of pros and cons. **Union** — the ability to connect: yourself with another, people with each other, sides that until then spoke different languages.

A strong 6 is quick to spot. Half an hour into a room full of strangers, this person knows who has fallen out with whom and is already sitting between them. They spend three weeks choosing a present, because a present has to be “about that person”. Their home has no random objects — or, on the contrary, is full of them, because choosing just one never quite happened. What matters to them is not only what is said but how. People like them, and they know it.

The 6 has one theme without which nothing else works: choosing yourself. Whoever finds it hard to choose themselves chooses the people who will approve of them, and calls it love. That is why the arcanum’s lesson is often put as self-love — meaning not vanity but the right to your own “I want” and “I don’t want” beside the people you love.

paragraphs: Lists of the 6’s minuses usually include words that sit badly with love: pessimism, cynicism, jealousy, fault-finding. They stop being surprising once you notice that almost every minus is a way of not choosing. There are three such ways.

**Not choosing.** Keeping both options open: two people, two jobs, two cities. It feels as if you lose nothing that way. In fact the options get tired of waiting, and the decision is made by someone else — a partner, a boss, circumstances. A postponed choice is a choice too, only not yours.

**Handing the choice to others.** Deciding the way parents, friends, colleagues or “normal people” would approve. The choice comes out right but belongs to someone else, and life inside it feels borrowed. Hence the resentment towards those who “made me”, although nobody made anyone do anything: they were simply handed the right to decide.

**Choosing an ideal instead of a person.** Falling in love with a picture and then measuring a living person against it. The picture never makes mistakes, never gets tired and is never in a bad mood — the living person loses to it every day. First comes criticism, then jealousy and control (“I’ll just check, in case he’s not who I think he is”), then the conclusion “they’re all the same”. A cynic with a 6 is a disappointed romantic: they loved the ideal for too long and decided not to love at all any more.
The plus of the 6 starts with the opposite move: make the choice, say so out loud, and stand by it when other options turn up.

sections.h2: Where the 6 sits in the matrix: check your date
paragraphs: In the destiny matrix, sums greater than 22 are reduced by adding up their digits. So a 6 comes not only from 6 but from 24, 33, 42 and even 51. Numbers up to 22 are not reduced, and this is where the most common mistake happens: **15 does not turn into 6**. Someone born on the 15th gets the fifteenth arcanum, The Devil, in their personality portrait, not The Lovers, as it would be in ordinary numerology. The same goes for years: 1950 gives 1 + 9 + 5 + 0 = 15, and that is The Devil again.

head: Point
When it is a 6
Share of people
rows: the sum A + B + C gives 6, 24, 33, 42 or 51
the sum A + B + C + D reduces to 6
calculated from the sums of the purposes

paragraphs: Example: 24 June 1986. Day 24 → 2 + 4 = 6, month 6, year 1 + 9 + 8 + 6 = 24 → 6. Three sixes in the outer points, and the karmic task is 6 + 6 + 6 = 18, The Moon.

85.0% of people have a 6 in at least one position of their reading — more than for any other arcanum: for the rest the figure ranges from 13.4 to 84.3%. That is arithmetic, not a mark of the chosen: several common sums reduce to 6 at once.

The 6 is even more noticeable in the spiritual purpose — one person in five has it there. This point has only seven possible values in the first place: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. That is how the sum it comes from is built. The same holds for point M, the entry of relationships and the tail. And in both points the 6 has a single cellmate: 15. If A + B + C leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 3, the spiritual purpose can only be 6 or 15; if the remainder is 2, the same thing happens at point M. The attraction that chooses and the attraction that binds share one seat in the chart.

The outer points also set the decades of life. For those born on the 6th and the 24th, childhood up to the age of 10 passes under The Lovers; for those born in June, the years from 20 to 30; for those born in the years from the table, the years from 40 to 50. 46.5% of people have at least one decade under the 6.

Several sixes in one chart do not mean “double love”. The record is ten points: for example, people born on 18 June 1971 have a 6 in the spiritual and karmic tasks and in all four family lines. Each of these sixes is read in its own role: one and the same theme of choice sounds now as an inner question, now as a family story, now as a money channel.

paragraphs: A year can also pass under the 6. It is a year of people and of choosing between them: options turn up on their own, and the year demands that you decide with whom and in what to invest. In detail: [on the year page](/year/6).

Next to other arcana the 6 changes its shade. With The Hanged Man (12) love gets stuck in waiting; with The Devil (15) attraction pulls hard and not always in the right direction; with The Hermit (9) the person reaches out to people and at once withdraws into themselves; with Strength (11) attraction turns into reliability. These and other pairs are covered on the combination pages: [6 and 12](/encyclopedia/combination/6-12), [6 and 15](/encyclopedia/combination/6-15), [6 and 9](/encyclopedia/combination/6-9), [6 and 11](/encyclopedia/combination/6-11).

sections.h2: Program 6: circling round the unchosen
paragraphs: A search for “program 6” means that a 6 stands in a point where the matrix reads repeating scripts. In our reading this is the section “Programs: what repeats in circles”, made of three lines: the karmic task D is the root of the storyline, the centre E is the state in which the autopilot switches on, and the spiritual purpose is the way out. 40.7% of people have a 6 in at least one of them. How programs work in general is covered on the [page about programs](/programs) and in the [report section](/encyclopedia/position/loops); here the subject is how the 6 in particular goes round.

Its loop is recognised by the ending: someone else makes the decision. A second option appears — a person, a job, a city. To choose means to disappoint someone, so the person stalls: tells both “almost yes”, waits for a sign, asks everyone’s advice. The options get tired of waiting. One leaves of its own accord, the other issues an ultimatum, or circumstances decide for everyone. What remains is the feeling “it’s always like this with me” — and next time the person is even more careful about choosing, which means they stall even longer. The storyline can be entirely mundane, too: spending six months choosing between two flats until both are let to someone else, or weighing two job offers for so long that both are withdrawn.
The role of the 6 depends on the line.

ul: **6 at the root (D).** A fork in the road sets the storyline going. Until the choice is made, life keeps handing it back: different people, the same question.

**6 in the centre (E).** Under pressure the autopilot is to adapt: to guess what the other person expects and become convenient. An early warning is the phrase “let’s do it your way”, said when you want something else.

**6 at the exit point (spiritual purpose).** This is the case for one person in five. Whatever the program is about — money, control, grievances — what helps to break the circle is a decision of the heart, spoken out loud, with a readiness to lose the other option.

paragraphs: You can test the program of the 6 against your own story. Recall two occasions when a decision was made for you, and ask yourself what you were doing the week before it was settled. If both times you were waiting, stalling and saying “no” to nobody, that is the one.

sections.h2: Karmic tails with a 6
paragraphs: The karmic tail is the set of three numbers in the lower part of the chart, read in the order M–N–D: entry, middle, root. 20.9% of people have a 6 in the tail, and it can take any of the three places:

ul: **at the entry (M)** the script starts with attraction — the wish to be liked, to be chosen, to fall in love;
**in the middle (N)** the loop is held together by a union — by a bond that is hard to let go of;
**at the root (D)** stands the task of the tail: to choose for yourself and to love a living person, not an image.

paragraphs: For dates since 1900 there are eight tails with a 6. In five of them it stands at the entry. When the 6 is in the middle, the entry is always The Moon (18): attraction seen by reflected light. Each tail has its own page:

sections.h2: 6 in compatibility: the 6 in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: Compatibility in the destiny matrix is not worked out by comparing two numbers. Tables like “6 goes well with 2, 4 and 14” compare arcana, not people. A couple’s matrix is built differently: the matching points of two personal matrices are added together and the sum is reduced to 1–22. A 6 appears in the couple’s matrix when the sum gives 6, 24, 33 or 42. For example, if one partner’s centre is 8 and the other’s is 16, the couple’s centre will be 8 + 16 = 24 → 6.

How the 6 reads in the couple’s points is described in detail by Yuliana Lisovskaya in her book “Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost” (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility). This is her own practice, not a general canon of the method. In summary:

ul: **In the couple’s centre** — the overall atmosphere. In the plus: tenderness, trust, talking about everything, deciding together even on small things, accepting each other’s imperfections. In the minus: a seesaw of “peace one day, war the next”, jealousy, words that wound.

**In the couple’s image point** (calculated from the partners’ birthdays) — how the couple looks from outside: beautiful, stylish, openly in love. In the minus: loud showdowns in public, or a smooth façade behind which nobody talks about what matters.

**In the couple’s tasks** — to stop idealising the relationship and remaking the partner to their own measure, to deal with the insecurity that jealousy and control grow out of, and to depend less on what the relatives think.
**In the couple’s money** — generosity and a love of the good life; in the minus, impulsive spending or gifts with strings attached.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentage. A 6 in a couple’s matrix describes what the union rests on and what it trips over, and says nothing about how it will all end.

sections.h2: The 6 for women and for men
paragraphs: The calculation is the same for a man and a woman: gender plays no part in the method, and people born on the same date have the same numbers. What differs is not the arcanum but the script the surroundings offer around it. This is about other people’s expectations, not about what a person is obliged to be.

A woman with a strong 6 is readily handed the role of the one who charms, reconciles and adorns. The trap is that “being liked” easily stands in for “choosing”: she becomes the one who gets chosen and fails to notice that she herself has not chosen anything for a long time. Her choices are also more often discussed by others — “she’s too picky”, “it’s time she made up her mind” — and a 6 in the minus hands the decision over to this chorus.

A man with a strong 6 more often has to defend what he has: taste, attention to people, a willingness to talk seriously about relationships. The trap is hiding it behind “I don’t mind, you choose”. It sounds accommodating, but in fact the choice has simply been shifted onto someone else — and the responsibility with it.

sections.h2: Waite’s Lovers: the picture on the card and where “choice” came from
paragraphs: On Waite’s card, drawn by Pamela Colman Smith in 1909, the sun stands at its zenith. Beneath it is a great winged figure with arms outstretched, which, in the author’s words, is “pouring down influences”. The angel is usually called Raphael, although Waite himself gives no name. Below are a naked man and woman, “as if Adam and Eve when they first occupied the paradise of the earthly body”. Behind the man stands the Tree of Life; behind the woman, the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, with the serpent twining round it. Between them, in the distance, a mountain rises.

Two details are worth a closer look. The Tree of Life in Waite’s description bears twelve fruits, like the tree of life in the Book of Revelation; in the drawing they look like tongues of flame. And the gazes: the man looks at the woman, and the woman looks up at the angel. In the twentieth century Paul Foster Case read this as a ladder: self-consciousness turns to subconsciousness, and subconsciousness to superconsciousness. Benebell Wen in “Holistic Tarot” sees in the man “the mind and rationality”, in the woman “the heart and emotion”, and in the card itself a choice “between the mind and the heart”.

Waite himself put the meaning briefly: “This is in all simplicity the card of human love” — of “youth, virginity, innocence and love before it is contaminated by gross material desire”, shown “as part of the way, the truth and the life”. “In a very high sense,” he adds, “the card is a mystery of the Covenant and Sabbath.” About the woman he writes separately: she is “rather the working of a Secret Law of Providence than a willing and conscious temptress”.

Choice came to this card from the old decks, and Waite argued with it. In fifteenth-century Italian decks the card was called Love (L’Amore): on the Milanese Visconti–Sforza cards a couple join hands as at a betrothal, and a blindfolded Cupid hovers above them. In the Tarot de Marseille it became L’Amoureux, “The Lover”, in the singular: a young man stands between two women, and Cupid takes aim downwards from a circle of sun. The women were read in different ways — as Vice and Virtue, after the story of Hercules at the crossroads, or as a mother and a bride. Waite saw in the old card a scene of married life, “shewing father and mother, with their child placed between them”, and called the later pictures “follies which depicted man between vice and virtue”. His own card, he says, replaces them “by recourse to first principles”: instead of a choice, Adam and Eve. The destiny matrix inherited both lines, Waite’s love and the Marseille tradition’s choice — hence the two words the 6 is known by.

For divination Waite gives the arcanum a short list. Upright: “Attraction, love, beauty, trials overcome.” Reversed: “Failure, foolish designs. Another account speaks of marriage frustrated and contrarieties of all kinds.” In the destiny matrix there are no reversed cards: a number taken from a date of birth lies neither upright nor upside down. Instead of the card’s position, the plus and the minus of the energy are read.

In the Golden Dawn system, to which Waite belonged, The Lovers is linked with the sign of Gemini. A coincidence, but an amusing one: Gemini covers the end of May and most of June, and in the destiny matrix people born in June get a 6 in the spiritual task.

And one more rhyme in Waite’s deck. The fifteenth arcanum, The Devil, repeats the composition of The Lovers: again a winged figure above, again a man and a woman below — but now with little horns and tails, chained to a pedestal. The chains round their necks are loose; they could be lifted off. It is the same scene of attraction, only here the choice has been given away. In the matrix these arcana are neighbours too: the points where either a 6 or a 15 falls are covered above, and their meeting in one chart is discussed in [the combination of 6 and 15](/encyclopedia/combination/6-15).

sections.h2: How to live the 6 in the plus
paragraphs: Working with the 6 always comes down to one skill: making a choice and holding to it. Here are five exercises, each with a time frame and a first step.

ol: **A decision with a date.** Take a choice that has been hanging for more than a month. Write down the options, set a decision day no more than two weeks away, and before that day tell the person it concerns. You may postpone again only out loud and with a new date.

**The secret ballot.** Before an important decision, answer on paper: what would I choose if no one ever found out about my choice? The gap between this answer and what you are about to do is the share of other people’s votes in the decision.

**A living person instead of a portrait.** Once a week, notice one thing someone close to you did differently from the picture you hold of them — and that you treasure in them. An ideal cannot do that; only a living person can.
**One “no” a week.** A 6’s “yes” is worth something only if it can also say “no”. Once a week, refuse where you would otherwise agree just so as not to disappoint.

**Choice in small things.** Every day, choose one thing purely on the principle “I like it”: a mug, the way home, the music in the car — without asking anyone’s opinion. The ability to choose is trained where a mistake costs nothing.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: The picture, symbolism and divinatory meanings of the card follow A. E. Waite’s “The Pictorial Key to the Tarot” (1922 reissue), illustrated by Pamela Colman Smith.
The reading of the card as a choice, and how it differs from The Devil, follow Benebell Wen’s “Holistic Tarot” (2015).
The 6 in a couple’s matrix follows Yuliana Lisovskaya’s “Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost” (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024).
The points are calculated by Natalia Ladini’s scheme. The shares of people were counted by the site’s engine over every date from 1 January 1900 to 5 October 2026.
The history of the card draws on the Visconti–Sforza decks (fifteenth century) and the Tarot de Marseille.

paragraphs: The destiny matrix is a system of interpretation, not a science: it describes tendencies and repeating scripts, but it does not predict events.

items.title: The Chariot
items.short: speed and drive: arrives first, as long as the reins are not dropped
meaning: The seventh arcanum is the energy of directed movement. If you reduce The Chariot to a single word, that word is “forward”: the number turns any task into a distance you have to cover before anyone else. What 7 means in the destiny matrix is a constant inner acceleration, where will, speed and hunger for a result are fused into one push — and that push needs a goal, or it starts to burn the person carrying it.

The inner motor of The Chariot is not ambition but the fear of stopping. Deep down lives the certainty: while I move, I am winning; the moment I stand still, I have lost. From there comes the number’s main conflict. Two forces pull the arcanum at once — the dash and the holding back — and the whole fate is decided by which of them leads. Power under control arrives first; the same power with no steering becomes a way to crash.

Being a seven is living with the motor always running. Thought outruns the conversation, a decision ripens before the details have been thought through, and other people’s calm reads as slowness. It is hard for such a person to believe that you can do nothing and still lose nothing; that feeling reaches The Chariot last of all, and usually at a high price.

The strong version of the number is gathered will: a clear goal, a chosen direction, and all the energy striking one point, so the seven gets through while others are still weighing things up. The weak version is the same power with no vector: thrill instead of sense, bravado instead of an outcome, constant tension because of everything standing in the way. The difference is not the size of the engine but whether it has a direction.

What sets The Chariot apart from its neighbours is action itself. The sixth arcanum, The Lovers, lives by choice and connection — it matters with whom and for whose sake; the seven dislikes choosing and wants to be driving already, and treats hesitation as time lost. The eighth arcanum, Justice, weighs things first: it hears both sides and only then gives its decision; The Chariot decides on the move and wins by pressure and pace. Where Justice stops to check the account, the seven pushes and overtakes.

in_positions.character: The pace gives them away at once: quick speech, quick decisions, a readiness to argue. This person is not interested in discussing things, they are interested in winning, and you can see it in the first five minutes of a conversation.
in_positions.comfort: Calm comes through movement: the road, sport, work for a result, a clear goal for the month. A forced stop feels like defeat, so “just rest for a while” does not work here.
in_positions.profession: A gift for carrying things through to a win. Their element is competition and a measurable result: sales, sport, launches, crisis projects. Slow desk work puts this talent out within six months. The Chariot needs a track with a finish line: a clear goal, a deadline, and the moment when the win is recorded and the next route can be chosen.
in_positions.realisation: The place for this arcanum is wherever a push is needed. They are meant to take on the hard, the disputed and the urgent, and carry it through. A quiet post with no challenge turns them into an irritated executor.
in_positions.karma40: For the Seven the age lens asks about managing speed. Without it the road can run through missed deadlines, broken relationships and projects abandoned halfway — until they learn to pick the route in advance.
in_positions.resources: The resource comes in through action and courage: first to sign up, first to take the risk, first to call. The condition is not to race blind: movement stalls where there is speed but no direction.
in_positions.family_gifts: Drive and staying power came down the family line. Someone lived through a war, a move, a start from nothing in a strange city — that force to break through was inherited and switches on at the critical moment. The run-up is handed over; the finish each person picks for themselves.
in_positions.soul_tasks: The inner work is about the price of a win. This arcanum knows how to win and does not always notice whom it knocked over on the way. The task is not to stop winning, but to see the people standing nearby.
in_positions.past_lives: They arrived with a habit of taking things by force and driving faster than needed. The power to break through is already trained: where others are still discussing, this person has done it. The pace is set without asking, disagreement reads as an obstacle, and little by little no one is left beside them. Before the next sprint, ask the person it touches: “are you with me at this pace?”
in_positions.purpose: The road here is a breakthrough of its own: to get through where everyone else stopped, and to lead others past that point. It can be sport, business, the army, any work that needs someone who will not back off.
in_positions.money: Earnings rest on speed and risk: deals, projects with a deadline, a percentage for the result. A salary with no competition kills motivation. The weak spot is losses from haste: they signed without reading to the end. Count the money twice before you sign — half an hour on a second reading of the contract is cheaper than any deal that falls apart.
in_positions.money40: Now the route matters more than the speed for the Seven: the same force aimed at one niche gives more than ten dashes in different directions. Experience has shown which road actually carries you, and a project built around one thing keeps going on its own. The run-up gathered over years is wiped out by the habit of dropping the wheel halfway and jumping to a new topic. Count how many directions you are running right now, and close all but one main one and one spare.
in_positions.relations: A partner gets fire, initiative and protection, and in return needs ground of their own. Long closeness holds up while both have movement; in a still relationship this arcanum starts fighting the partner out of boredom. Closeness does not have to move at the speed of that run-up, and a step put off by one conversation saves more than the pace gained.
in_positions.parents_children: The demand at home was short: a result, pull yourself together, no whining. The same tone switches on with whoever they lead — plenty of movement and a high bar. The other half is needed too: the right to lose without a debriefing, otherwise the younger one beside them grows up afraid to try.
in_positions.ancestry: What the family line needs from this person is a finish. The elders stopped half a step short of the result — they are the ones asked to get there and show that it can be done. Take one “almost ready” thing and close it this week, even if it comes out more modest than planned.
in_positions.body_resource: The Chariot holds up under load: sport, the road, work with their hands. An even state shows itself in the evening — if there was somewhere to spend the force during the day, they are calm and not looking for someone to argue with. Without movement the energy turns into irritation, and what breaks this arcanum is not the work but having nowhere to burn it off; lying down is no rest for them. Limit one task by time, finish it at the agreed point, and compare that evening with an ordinary day with no finish.
in_positions.chakras: The Chariot: at this level arcanum 7 gives what is its own — carrying things to the goal where the rest stop. When it tips, the win arrives with no force left for joy. The practical check for this level is to pick not only the speed but the direction too.
in_positions.rest: Rest works when it is active: mountains, water, speed, a contest for the fun of it. Lying by the sea lasts two days, then they start hunting for something to do and spoil the holiday for everyone. Movement restores them while it stays a pleasure; as soon as a score and a result appear, a second job begins.
in_positions.loops: The story repeats as a run-up and a crash: they picked up the pace, swept the obstacles away, lost the people and stood alone at the finish. The way out is to decide in advance what must not be broken in this race.
in_positions.years: Ten years of the Chariot are a road with fast-changing scenery: a move, a career jump, a business of their own, sport. Speed pays off where a finish has been chosen: it is clear where we are going and what will count as arrival. With no finish chosen the movement is just tiredness — many kilometres, and nothing to show. Check the route once a year and write down what really shifted in that time.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 7 — The Chariot: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: Arcanum 7, The Chariot, is the energy of will, speed and victory. What 7 means in the destiny matrix: its character, its engine, its strong and weak versions.

article.title: The 7th arcanum in the destiny matrix: The Chariot
article.short: Seven in the destiny matrix is The Chariot, the arcanum of directed will. It gives you the knack of gathering yourself and your circumstances into a single movement and driving it through to victory, especially where others have already stopped. It has one weak spot, too: The Chariot wins in the outer world, but questions like “why?” and “what do I actually feel?” are not settled by speed. Below: how the seven looks in the plus and in the minus, which plot it keeps replaying, which points and tails it turns up in, and what Waite wrote about it.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 7: The Chariot — meaning, program, karmic tail
seo.description: Destiny matrix 7 is The Chariot, will with a direction: its plus and minus, how to break the loop of program 7, four karmic tails and the 7 in a couple.

sections.h2: What 7 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: The Chariot is the seventh of the 22 major arcana, and its meaning fits into a short formula: will with a direction. Plenty of arcana have energy; what sets the seven apart is a course. A person with a strong 7 can name a goal, gather time, money, people and themselves around it — and get there.

The Chariot does not move because everything inside agrees. “I want” and “I’m scared”, “I must” and “I don’t feel like it”, calculation and resentment all pull in different directions, and the seven can make the parts that disagree move one way. Its strength is steering a contradiction, not living without one. That is why these people often find their footing in a crisis: when everything falls apart for others, they finally have a job to do.

For the seven, the road is never sightseeing. Benebell Wen, author of Holistic Tarot, describes The Chariot as “travel not for the sake of travel, but for the sake of acquisition”. Moving for a job, a business trip to close a deal, a climb to the summit — the seven always travels to fetch something.

In the deck, The Chariot comes straight after The Lovers (6): there you choose, here you drive on the choice. The seventh arcanum is a decision already being carried out, with all its pluses (things are moving) and minuses (it is too late for doubts).

Arthur Edward Waite, whose design lies behind the best-known tarot deck, singled out two things in this card, and the whole of the seven in the matrix rests on them. First, the victory is won, not handed down: the hero of the card, in his words, “is not hereditary royalty and he is not priesthood”. Second, the victory belongs to the outer world and the mind, and it does not yet mean the victor has mastered himself. The seven’s standing is earned; its weak spot lies within.

**In short.** The strength: carrying things through to a result. The weakness: not knowing how to stop and not seeing the cost. The task: knowing in advance where you are going and what will count as arriving.

sections.h2: Seven in the plus and in the minus
paragraphs: The same energy in different hands looks like leadership or like a battering ram. Here is how to tell them apart in everyday life.

head: Where it shows
In the plus
In the minus
rows: Decides fast once the goal is clear and does not reopen the decision at every step
Decides before understanding the goal, then defends the decision like territory
Finishes what others gave up on; strong at launches, crunch time, moves and competitions
Takes on five things and drops them halfway; measures life by a speed report
Speaks plainly, takes a hit, stands up for their own
Wins the argument and loses the person; won’t give way even on trifles
Pulls the couple forward, acts when someone close is struggling
Treats feelings as problems to solve; the partner rides along as a passenger nobody asked
Recharges through movement: the road, sport, a change of scene
A pause feels like losing; a holiday turns into an itinerary
Earns on results: a project, a deal, a percentage
Rushes, takes risks, borrows for the next push

paragraphs: The seven’s minus comes in two kinds, and they are easy to mistake for different arcana. The first is the overheated Chariot: it drives, presses, flattens, abandons. The second is the Chariot stuck in park: there is no goal, the power has nowhere to go and turns into irritation, nitpicking and quarrels out of nothing. From outside the second one looks like laziness, but it is an engine without a road. Both have the same way out — a goal worth travelling for, not the ride itself.

Even in Waite’s old fortune-telling list, The Chariot puts “succour, providence” right next to “war, presumption, vengeance”. It is one power: turned towards people, it comes to the rescue; turned against them, it goes to war.

sections.h2: Victory outside, the question within
paragraphs: The most interesting thing about the seven shows not in its victories but in what victory cannot take. Waite describes the hero of the card as a triumph of the mind: he is “conquest on all planes — in the mind, in science, in progress”. Then he spends almost a whole paragraph listing where that victory runs out. Here are three of Waite’s points that are easy to recognise in life.

**Solves problems, not mysteries.** In Waite, the victor answers the riddles of Nature but not the questions of Grace. In everyday terms: the seven is strong wherever a problem yields to effort — pass, build, move, win, pull someone out. And it is lost where there is nothing to solve: grief, falling in love, faith, forgiveness. Someone close is crying, and five minutes later they are handed a three-point plan. The plan is good. The person was not waiting for a plan.

**Frees others, stays captive himself.** Another of Waite’s caveats: the liberation the victor brings “may leave himself in the bondage of the logical understanding”. A familiar picture: someone has pulled a brother out of debt, moved their parents, rescued a colleague’s deadline, and when asked “but what do you want?”, answers with a to-do list for the week.

**The crown has to be won again.** Waite writes that The Chariot is really “the King in his triumph”: the victory that creates kingship as its natural consequence, unlike the vested crown of The Emperor (4). Hence the seven’s particular feeling: respect does not keep, it has to be earned again every time. The Emperor can sit on the throne. The Chariot, to stay itself, has to keep moving, and that is at once its gift and its trap.

Wen adds a psychological detail. She links the card to the sign of Cancer: “tough on the outside, but deep down… quite vulnerable and sensitive”. Such a person likes to appear in control, yet has two habitual escapes from anything hard — to run from the problem, or to attack it with such aggression that the real conversation never has to happen. The third way — staying and talking it through — is the hardest and the most grown-up for the seven.
A mature seven does not slow down. It learns to tell the problems that need winning from the questions that need living through.

sections.h2: Where the seven stands and what it does there
paragraphs: The seven is no rarity: 81.2% of people have it somewhere in their reading. So what matters is not the fact but the place: The Chariot in the calling card, in the centre and on the money line says different things. The shares below are counted over every date of birth from 1900 to 2026.

How many people
What the seven does

Its footing is movement: without a task the person loses shape faster than from tiredness. [More on the seven in the centre](/encyclopedia/position/center/7)
