ul: **Spiritual task, point B.** This is the month of birth, and there are only twelve months. For the same reason 13 never leads the decade from 20 to 30: the age scale takes that decade from the month.
**Entry of relationships and the tail, point M.** Only multiples of three stand there. So neither the tail nor the relationship line ever starts with 13.
**Spiritual and social purpose.** Of the four purposes, 13 occurs only in the personal and the planetary.

paragraphs.h3: Where 13 depends directly on the date

ul: **Calling card** — only for people born on the 13th. Other days don’t reduce to 13: the 23rd gives 5, the 31st gives 4.

**Material task, point C** — calculated from the sum of the digits of the birth year. Only 1903, 1912, 1921 and 1930 give 13; the next such year is 2029. So the decade from 40 to 50 falls under 13 only for people born in those years.

sections.h2: 13 in the calling card and the comfort zone
paragraphs: The calling card is the birth day arcanum, point A, the [personality portrait](/encyclopedia/position/day): what people read in you before they get to know you. 13 stands here only for those born on the 13th of any month — roughly three people in a hundred.

Conversations with such a person turn serious fast. People tell them about their divorce at the second meeting and ask their advice when deciding whether to quit or move away. Around them you don’t have to pretend everything is fine. They change visibly rather than gradually: a sharp change of image, profession or city comes more naturally to them than a straight line.

In the minus, a 13 calling card is a heavy seriousness and black humour that hide the person behind them, or a reputation for vanishing without explanation. The age scale starts from the same point, so for people born on the 13th, 13 also leads the first decade of life. The reading treats it as a childhood in which you have to learn change and goodbyes early.

[13 in the centre of the matrix](/encyclopedia/position/center/13) — for 4% of people. The centre is also called the comfort zone: the state in which a person feels like themselves. With 13 in the centre, you feel at ease not when nothing changes but after a clear-out — when what has had its day is gone and there is room for the new. The full reading is on its own page.

You can watch 13 reach the centre on the date 13 March 1975. The centre is the sum of the four outer points: the day (13), the month (3), the year (1 + 9 + 7 + 5 = 22) and the karmic task (11). That makes 49, and 4 + 9 = 13. Here 13 sits at two points at once — the calling card and the centre. And a curious detail: everyone with 13 in the centre has the same karmic tail — [6-17-11](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-17-11).

The centre also plays a part in the section on rest. 13 recovers not on the sofa but through change: another city for the weekend, a cleared-out wardrobe, a sauna after a hard week, a new haircut, a long road. For 13, rest is a small ending: shedding what has built up so that there is room again.

sections.h2: The talent of 13: careers and work you love
paragraphs: The talent line in the matrix runs through three points, and the first of them is the month, so 13 can only appear at the second and third: the [middle point of talent](/encyclopedia/position/profession) or the [inner point of talent K](/encyclopedia/position/comfort_north). In the section on profession, 13 appears for 11.3% of people.

The talent of 13 is to work where something is ending and to give that ending meaning. In any team, this is the person called in to close a failing project, relaunch a product, carry out a painful restructuring and say out loud what everyone knows and nobody says.
Where this talent fits best:

ul: **closing things down:** turnaround management, bankruptcy and company liquidation, restructuring, divorce and probate lawyers, notaries. Wen mentions that tradition links this card with “property and inheritance”;
**guiding people through transitions:** psychologists who work with grief and crisis, palliative care, career coaches for people changing profession, relocation specialists;
**removing what is surplus:** editing of text and film, surgery, demolition, recycling and disposal, organising spaces;
**giving the old a second life:** restoration, antiques, repair and resale, archives, history.

paragraphs: The same tradition sets death and birth side by side — which is why midwifery also turns up in lists of careers for 13: work at the door through which people come in. So does work close to literal death: funeral services, forensic medicine. 13 stays calmer there than most people do.

In the minus, the talent turns against its owner: a person sits for ten years in a job that ended in its first year, or changes jobs every twelve months as soon as boredom sets in. Both mistakes come down to the same thing — they cannot tell an ending from a difficult middle.

sections.h2: 13 in money and the money channel
paragraphs: In the money section, 13 appears for 9.7% of people. Most often it stands at the [entry of the money line](/encyclopedia/position/comfort_east) or at its middle point — where the matrix shows where money comes from and how. The money points as a whole are covered in the article on [money in the matrix](/encyclopedia/position/money).

For 13, money comes after closing something down. While a person keeps dragging along a loss-making project, a job they dislike or a flat that only eats money, the channel is taken up by something dead. Once they end it, what frees up is not only time but room for income. Typical sources of that income are a change of field, a second profession, work with other people’s crises, and things and spaces given a second life.

The main money trap for 13 is pity for what has already gone in. “So much effort has gone into it, I can’t just drop it” keeps people in dead ventures for years. The opposite trap is resetting to zero without a cushion: quitting into nothing, putting everything into one risky idea, starting with a clean slate and an empty account.

Yuliana Lisovskaya, the author of a book on compatibility in the matrix, advises couples with 13 to build a financial cushion in advance. For an individual with 13 in money, a cushion is not stinginess either but the right to end things on time: to leave a dead job when it becomes clear it is time, not when you finally find the courage.

In the section on money after 40, 13 appears for 6.7% of people. There 13 reads as a second career: the experience of the first becomes the capital of the next rather than a weight around your ankles.

sections.h2: 13 in relationships
paragraphs: In the relationships section, 13 appears for 9.1% of people. It cannot start the [relationship line](/encyclopedia/position/relations) — it never appears at the entry point M — but it does occur at the partner point R1, labelled “Under the heart”, at the crossing of the money and relationship lines and at the inner point of talent. The partner point has a page of its own: [13 under the heart](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/13).

Love with 13 is deep and wears no masks: with it you can’t keep a polite distance for years. Its main strength in a couple is the ability to change form without losing the bond. The passion of the early years, shared everyday life, small children, grown children who have moved away — each stage buries the one before. With 13 you can have several marriages to the same person: the couple lives through the end of the old form and builds a new one instead of splitting up.
It also knows how to end things honestly. It doesn’t stay “friends in hope”, doesn’t drag a past love into a new one, and accepts a partner’s past: they had a life before you, and that is fine.

In the minus — the same two extremes. Some live for years in relationships that have died, “for the children”, “for the flat”, “because we’re used to it”. Others leave at the first crisis and never give the couple a chance to change its form. Before deciding, one question helps: what exactly has ended — the love, or its old form? If it is the form, you can bury it and stay together.

sections.h2: 13 in compatibility: the energy a couple gives birth to
paragraphs: Compatibility in the matrix is calculated in different ways; here it follows the school of Yuliana Lisovskaya and her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (The Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). The couple’s matrix is built like this: the matching points of the two people are added together, and the sum is reduced to a number from 1 to 22.

Hence an unexpected property of 13. At any point of a couple’s matrix, 13 comes only from a sum of exactly 13 — for example 6 and 7, 4 and 9, or 1 and 12. No other sum reduces to 13. So each partner has a number below thirteen at that point: neither of them has their own Death there. A couple doesn’t bring 13 with it; it gives birth to it. Lisovskaya discusses a couple with 13 at two points, although neither partner has 13 at all, and reads it as an experience the two of them live through for the first time — together.
What 13 means in a couple, according to Lisovskaya:

ul: **in the plus:** the couple often has a past — not a first marriage, children from earlier relationships — and the partners accept each other’s past. Trips, moves and everything new fill them up. They are decisive: they may marry quickly and have children soon. One helps the other get out of something destructive — an addiction or a toxic relationship;
**in the minus:** emotional swings; so much change that whoever needs stability suffers; one tries to remake the other; traits of former partners are carried over onto the current one;
**the couple’s tasks:** to separate from their parents, buy a home or move, endure distance and time apart, live through crises as a test and see their own mistakes, not only the other’s;
**money:** in the plus, the ability to save and always keep a reserve; in the minus, fear of changing jobs and resentment of the partner’s growth.

paragraphs: These are possible scenarios of the energy, not facts about a particular couple. The method gives no compatibility percentages, and 13 in a couple’s matrix is not a verdict on the relationship but its theme: a union that can live through endings and start again without parting.

sections.h2: 13 in karma and the karmic tail
paragraphs: There are 26 possible karmic tails in the matrix, and 13 appears in only two of them. It cannot start a tail — the tail’s first point, M, is always a multiple of three. That leaves two options:

ul: [21-7-13](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/21-7-13) — Death at the end of the tail, at point D. If you have 13 at point D, this is always your tail;
[3-13-10](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/3-13-10) — Death in the middle of the tail. If 13 sits at its middle point, this is always your tail.

paragraphs: Together that is 1.8% of people. Both tails carry frightening nicknames in popular lists, and both are covered on their own pages — calmly and without labels.

Point D itself, the [karmic task](/encyclopedia/position/mission), holds 13 for 1.5% of people. The task here is to learn to end things: not to hold on to what is dead and not to cut down what is alive. The same point leads the decade from 60 to 70 and takes part in the sections on spiritual lessons and on the programs that repeat in circles.

The karmic theme opens up more widely in the section “Karmic task before 40”: there 13 appears for 9.2% of people. The first half of life tests whether you can leave what is spent — your parents’ script, your first profession, your first marriage if it has ended. You don’t have to leave; you do have to answer honestly whether what you are staying in is still alive.

If 13 lands in the [programs](/encyclopedia/position/loops), the repetition shows in identical endings: work grows dull at the same point every time, relationships break over the same quarrel, moves come every three years. The program loosens its hold once one such ending is lived through fully — with a farewell, not an escape.

sections.h2: 13 in the family line
paragraphs: The family sections are among the places where 13 turns up most: in the gifts of the family line it appears for 12.8% of people, in family tasks for 11.2%, in the karma of relationships with parents and children for 10.7%. It stands on one of the four family lines — [spiritual male](/encyclopedia/position/father_line), [spiritual female](/encyclopedia/position/mother_line), [material male](/encyclopedia/position/descendants) or [material female](/encyclopedia/position/inheritance) — or in the total of one of the branches.

13 in the family line is read as a history of upheavals: moves, ruptures, losses, lives that had to be started again from nothing. The stories of many families in the last century had no shortage of such upheavals. As a gift, it is the family’s ability to rise after an ending: you have been handed the capacity not to break when the familiar world comes to an end.

As a task, 13 asks you to finish what the family left unfinished: losses that were never mourned, subjects the family keeps silent about, quarrels that have dragged on for generations. Sometimes the task is simpler and harder at once: to be the one with whom the old family script ends. If, generation after generation, your family cuts people off for good or, the other way round, puts up with what is dead to the very last, the cycle can stop with you.

In relationships with parents, 13 speaks of a separation that needs to happen: separating without breaking off. With children, it speaks of teaching them to end things: to say goodbye, to let go and to live through losses rather than hide them. A child who was allowed to grieve grows into an adult who is not afraid of endings.

sections.h2: 13 in the chakras, across the decades and in purpose
paragraphs: The chakra map is where 13 appears most often: 45.9% of people have it there. The map lays out a person’s strengths across seven levels, from the body and grounding up to a connection with the bigger design, and each level has physics, energy and emotions. 13 at a level means that strength returns there through letting go: in grounding, through changing an established way of life; in love, through bringing old feelings to a close; in speech, through being able to say “no” and “that’s it”. How to read your own map is explained in the section on [chakras](/encyclopedia/position/chakras).

In the [reading by decades](/encyclopedia/position/years), 13 leads at least one decade for 21.8% of people. The scale moves through eight points, ten years each, and 13 can stand almost anywhere except in two places: 20–30 is the month of birth, and 40–50 is the year, where 13 occurs only for those born in 1903, 1912, 1921 and 1930.

A decade under 13 is read as a time when a big chapter closes. Your age will suggest which one: at 10–20 it is a goodbye to childhood and the parental home, at 30–40 a rebuild of your first adult life, at 50–60 a way out of roles held for decades, at 70–80 a time to take stock and let go. This is a direction, not a schedule of events.

A personal year under arcanum 13 has its own page — [13 for the year](/year/13). In short, it is a year of parting with the old, and it goes more easily if you let go of what has had its day yourself, without waiting for life to do it for you.

Of the four purposes, 13 occurs in the personal (for 0.9% of people) and the [planetary](/encyclopedia/position/planetary) (for 2.9%). Wen calls 13 “the card of revolutions” — the waning of one authority and the rise of another. In planetary purpose, this is the role of someone who helps the world around them let go of the outdated: reform, close down old orders, guide people through change.

sections.h2: How 13 differs from The Tower and other arcana of change
paragraphs: Several arcana in the matrix speak of change, and they are easy to confuse. The difference lies in what exactly ends, and how.

sections.h2: Waite’s Death card: the rider with no weapon
paragraphs: Older decks drew the thirteenth bluntly. Waite himself describes this canon: the field of life, with “living arms and heads protruding from the ground”, one of the heads crowned, and “a skeleton with a great scythe” mowing them down. The meaning, in his words, is “transparent and unescapable” — death; interpreters added change and transformation to it, but in its plain sense it is rather “a card of the death of Kings”.

In the 1909 deck that Pamela Colman Smith drew to his design, Waite replaced “the crude notion of the reaping skeleton” with one of the apocalyptic visions. A skeleton in black armour rides slowly on a white horse and “carries no visible weapon”. He bears a black banner with the white Mystic Rose, “which signifies life”. Before him “king and child and maiden fall”, while “a prelate with clasped hands awaits his end”. On the horizon, between two pillars, shines “the sun of immortality”.
What this means for the matrix:

ul: **No weapon.** Death does not attack here. It is not an enemy that comes to take something away but the passage of time, which cannot be stopped. Fighting an ending is pointless; how you meet it is up to you.

**A rose on black.** A sign of life on the banner of the end: completion carries continuation inside it. Waite’s own verdict points the same way: he found the readings “rebirth, creation, destination, renewal” for this card “on the whole, better than usual”.

**The king is already down.** Power buys no reprieve — and neither do innocence or prayer. Wen writes that the card is a reminder that “no one is above suffering. King and peasant alike deal with pain and affliction.”

**Three answers to an ending.** The child looks straight at the rider, the maiden turns away, the prelate meets him with prayer. It is easy to see three ways of meeting change here: openly, by turning away, and through ritual.

**The sun between the towers.** Beyond the ending there is a horizon. Wen notes that rider and horse are marching “in the direction of the rising sun, though that sun is still far in the distance”: a transition takes time.

paragraphs: The card is traditionally linked with Scorpio and the element of Water. From this Wen draws advice for anyone who is stuck: to “be fluid like water” — not to break against change but to flow around it.

sections.h2: Living 13 in the plus: seven rules for a good ending
paragraphs: 13 doesn’t ask you to break anything. It asks you to stop pretending that what is dead is alive — and not to bury what is alive before its time. In practice it looks like this.

ol: **Name the ending out loud.** Dead forms most often live on because nobody has said “this is over”. Say it to yourself first, then to the people it concerns.

**Separate the form from the substance.** The form ends, but what is valuable moves on: skills from the job you left, friends from the circle that broke up, closeness from a marriage that has turned into a partnership of parents. Before the ending, make a list of what you are taking with you.

**Give it one try.** If you tend to cut, then before deciding, name one thing you will still try to fix and a deadline after which you will stop. An ending that follows an honest attempt doesn’t torment you with “what if”.
**Finish the small things.** Keys, debts, the handover, words of thanks. An unfinished ending drags on for years; a finished one lets you go.
**Grieve.** Sadness is not a sign of a mistake but the very work of completion. Give it time: without it the ending doesn’t arrive, it only gets postponed.

**Don’t jump straight into the new.** After the thirteenth arcanum comes the fourteenth, Temperance: the new blends in slowly. A new relationship a week after a break-up is often an attempt to skip the ending.

**Take stock once a season.** What in my life is alive only out of habit? Work, subscriptions, commitments, conversations, roles. Whoever ends things a little at a time seldom has to cut everything at once.

paragraphs: An ending is work too, and 13 knows how to do it. Whoever has learned to end things stops being afraid to begin.

items.title: Temperance
items.short: measure and blending: joins what does not join and keeps an even pace
meaning: The fourteenth arcanum in the destiny matrix is the energy of measure and of joining. What 14 means: by nature such a person mixes and evens things out — takes two forces that will not meet and finds the right proportion between them. The easiest way to grasp it is the picture on the card, where an angel pours liquid from one cup into another without spilling a drop: 14 makes nothing new out of emptiness and tears nothing old down to the ground, it brings what already exists into one even flow.

This energy believes that the truth lies in the middle and that extremes do harm. From there come both its main strength and its pace: where others throw themselves from fire into ice, the fourteenth dilutes one with the other and keeps an even current. Such an arcanum plays the long game: a steady stride overtakes the bursts that burn out fast. Its engine is not passion or pressure, but an exact dose and patience.

Living as this arcanum means feeling other people’s tension all the time and reaching out to smooth it. From the inside it works like being a pair of scales: you hold the balance between the sides, and the better you hold it, the less anyone notices what it costs. Here the main conflict hides: forever levelling out what is around them, a person stops hearing their own tilt — their own wish, which is exactly the “extreme” they are used to diluting.

A strong fourteen is the master of proportion: it brings people and processes together, carries long things through to a result and still stays itself. The weak version is when measure degrades into half-measures: afraid of tipping the cup, a person never goes all the way with anything and ends up with lukewarm water instead of a living taste. The difference between the versions is not in the power of the number, but in the willingness to choose something whole at least once instead of blending it down to a safe middle.

From its neighbours in the deck the fourteenth differs by refusing sharpness. The thirteenth, Death, cuts off and resets to zero — 14 tears nothing, it moves one state into another smoothly. The fifteenth, The Devil, lives on passion and excess and takes at once — Temperance dilutes that excess on purpose and waits for the right proportion. Where others act by force or by a sudden push, the fourteenth wins by patience and an exact measure.

in_positions.character: A steady, calm person; next to them the tension in a room drops. They do not rush to extremes, hear both sides and almost always find a middle road that suits everyone.
in_positions.comfort: What fills them up is an even pace: their own tempo, a familiar day, work without a race. Sharp changes and rush jobs knock this centre out, while one quiet week puts almost everything back.
in_positions.profession: The gift is joining what will not join. They work where things have to be reconciled and tuned: mediation, people management, repair and restoration, teaching, any long process. Roles built on conflict and constant pressure are hard for them. Their work is like tuning a complicated instrument: the value is heard not in one bright burst, but in scattered parts finally sounding together.
in_positions.realisation: Moving forward here means holding the proportion where everyone else falls into extremes. Such a person walks long and evenly; measuring themselves against people who shoot up in a single year makes no sense.
in_positions.karma40: The earliest grown-up decisions teach the fourteenth arcanum not to live by halves. They are afraid to tip the scales, so the road can stick in compromises: no quarrel, no decision, no voice of their own. The new answer is to choose fully at least once.
in_positions.resources: Constancy is what brings the inflow: a little at a time, but always. The condition is not to drop things halfway and not to push for speed — this arcanum gets nowhere in bursts, and gets almost everything at an even pace.
in_positions.family_gifts: Peacemaking came down the line, and with it the skill of keeping ties. Somewhere in the family line there was a person everyone else talked through, and the gift still works, especially at big gatherings. What is worth repeating is not their sacrifice but their method: join the extremes without becoming the target between them.
in_positions.soul_tasks: The delicate subject is their own wanting. By constantly diluting the hot with the cold, a person stops understanding what they want themselves. The inner work here is to take back the right to an extreme.
in_positions.past_lives: The old training is to smooth things over and touch nobody. The ability to join what does not join is real: around such a person there is no storm. Their own wish dissolves in compromise, and instead of a decision an even nothing comes out. In one question, take your own side openly and stop looking for the middle.
in_positions.purpose: Here the road runs through bringing balance back and tuning: putting in order what has drifted apart — people, processes, one’s own rhythm. The work is slow, but the result holds for years.
in_positions.money: Money comes here for long steady work: support, repair, teaching, anything that takes patience. Quick schemes do not suit this arcanum, while a stable flow it holds better than most. Set up one repeating payment — a pass, a subscription, a monthly contract — and leave the terms alone for at least six months.
in_positions.money40: By forty this arcanum arrives with a built-up client base and a reputation for being calm. An even pace held for years brings people by itself: they come back to someone who does not blow up and does not disappear. Income does not grow from age alone — the base ages if it is not refreshed, and in five years it brings in half as much. Call five clients who have not been in touch for over a year and offer them something new.
in_positions.relations: With a partner like this it is calm: they are patient, make no scenes and know how to come to terms. The risk is lukewarm water: a bond with no passion and no conversations, because nobody dares to start them. Warmth here rests on small repeated things, and that only becomes visible a year or two later.
in_positions.parents_children: At home it was even and without shouting, and a conflict counted as something unnecessary. That evenness passes on: a child feels calm beside this person, who never raises their voice. What is sometimes missing is a clear “no” — this arcanum avoids collisions and so leaves the boundaries blurred.
in_positions.ancestry: Reconciliation is what this line is waiting for. Relatives have scattered into different camps, and their role is to be the one who gets everybody back around one table. Make one step towards them, but do not appoint yourself responsible for making peace between people who do not want it.
in_positions.body_resource: Temperance holds best on a quiet rhythm: a familiar walk, an ordinary supper and one pace for several days running work better than a rare big push. You can see it in a boring but living picture: the same road, the same hour given to a task, and by Friday there is as much strength as there was on Tuesday. What lets them down is the belief that since everything runs evenly, the load can be doubled: a week at double load ends in a slump after which the old pace feels impossible. It is useful to pick one realistic rhythm for a week and not raise it even on the day when you want to do everything at once.
in_positions.chakras: Temperance: the level works through the theme of measure — joining what will not join without losing the shape. The strong move is to find the proportion in which everything works; the failure looks like middling where a choice was needed. One thing brings the footing back: measure by the result, not by an avoided extreme.
in_positions.rest: Rest works when it is gentle and regular: water, walks, a spa-like rhythm, quiet trips. Extreme sports and loud parties do not put this arcanum back together, they shake it loose. The value of such rest shows up not in the moment but the next day, in an even state rather than in bright stories.
in_positions.loops: Half-measures are what go round in this life: did not say it, did not leave, did not start — and everything stayed as it was for another three years. The way out is one full decision taken without dilution.
in_positions.years: Years of Temperance look less like fireworks and more like an even flame: study, relationships and work settle slowly and without strain. There are few sharp events, but a margin of strength builds up: a habit held for years gives more than three bursts in a row. The even course is knocked off by swinging between extremes, and also by a cosy standstill that is easy to mistake for measure. Pick one pace, hold it for a month, and at the end note what managed to change.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 14 — Temperance: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: Measure, an even pace and joining things: that is arcanum 14, Temperance. What it means in the destiny matrix, in its strong and weak versions.

article.title: Arcanum 14 in the destiny matrix: Temperance and the art of measure
article.short: 14 in the destiny matrix is the Temperance arcanum. It is the energy of the right proportion: the skill of joining two different principles so that neither is lost, keeping a pace you can sustain for years, and letting what matters ripen. Temperance here is not “a little of everything”, and not softness either, but what makes the hard durable and the different compatible. In the plus, 14 brings a sense of measure, taste and a rare knack for reconciling the irreconcilable. In the minus, it brings the lukewarm water of endless compromise, or a seesaw from one extreme to the other.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 14: meaning of the Temperance arcanum
seo.description: Destiny matrix 14 is Temperance, the arcanum of right proportion: character, talent, money and love, where 14 sits in a chart and where it never can.

sections.h2: What 14 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: If you had to sum up the arcanum in one sentence: 14 knows how much of each thing is needed. Not equal shares, but the right proportion. A pinch of salt in a pot of soup is measure; half salt, half soup is not. A person with a strong 14 senses such proportions almost physically: how much to talk and how much to listen, how much to work and how much to rest, how much of your own to give up so that something shared can come of it — and where giving way is no longer an option.
The arcanum holds three skills, and they depend on one another:

ul: **Mixing.** Joining different things — people, tastes, habits, skills — so that a third thing appears that neither side had on its own.
**Measuring.** Finding a proportion and a pace that can be held for a long time: not a sprint and not a standstill, but an even stride.
**Waiting.** Understanding that some things have their own time to ripen, and not poking the dough while it rises.

paragraphs: Arthur Edward Waite, the author of the best-known tarot deck, wrote that the rule of this card “tempers, combines and harmonises the psychic and material natures” of a person — the inner and the outer. Benebell Wen, the author of Holistic Tarot, draws a precise line between it and its neighbour: Justice stands for external balance, while Temperance “is about internal balance”, when two contrasting elements fuse into one.

The arcanum is common: 14 stands somewhere in the matrix report of 68.9% of people, about two in three. For comparison, the rarest arcana appear in the charts of 13% of people, the most frequent in 85%. But at different points 14 does different things, and that is what follows.

sections.h2: Measure is proportion, not the middle
paragraphs: “Temperance” sounds modest, almost dull: a temperate climate, a moderate appetite, moderate views. The Latin word the card’s name comes from is far richer. Temperare means “to mix in the right proportion”. A whole family of words grows from the same root, and each one explains the arcanum better than any definition.

ul: **Temperature** originally meant “due mixture” — the ratio of warm to cold.
**Temperament** in ancient theory was the blend of a person’s four “humours”. Character was understood as a proportion, not as a list of traits.
**Tempera** is paint in which the pigment is mixed with egg yolk. For centuries it was used to paint icons and pictures on wooden panels.

**Tempered tuning** is a way of tuning in which every interval departs ever so slightly from the “pure” one, but no key sounds out of tune. In 1722 Bach wrote The Well-Tempered Clavier — preludes and fugues in all 24 keys — to show that it could be done. A piano tuner, in effect, still tempers today.

**Tempering** is also what metalworkers call the step after hardening. Freshly hardened steel is hard but brittle — a blow can crack it. It is heated again, moderately, and it keeps its hardness but stops breaking.

paragraphs: The last example is the key to 14. Temperance does not cancel strength; it makes strength durable: the hard without measure cracks, the soft without measure spreads. Bronze is harder than both the copper and the tin it is made from: a blend in the right proportion gives a quality that none of its parts had.

In English, temperance also means abstinence from drink — the temperance societies of the nineteenth century took their name from it. But the card is some four hundred years older than that meaning and speaks not of prohibition but of mixing. In the old list of virtues, temperance meant not giving up wine but knowing how to dilute it: the Greeks considered drinking undiluted wine a habit of barbarians.

paragraphs.h3: A card of time and of art

paragraphs: 14 has other names, too. The Russian philosopher Pyotr Ouspensky, in his book Simvoly Taro (The Symbolism of the Tarot, 1912), called this card “Time”. Wen notes that “in notable twentieth-century texts” it is called the Time card. Aleister Crowley renamed it “Art” in his Thoth deck — and that, too, is about proportion: every craft begins with knowing how much of each thing to put in and how long to wait.
Hence the three words the arcanum rests on: blend, measure, time.

sections.h2: What 14 looks like in real life
paragraphs: **The dinner table.** People who would never cross paths in ordinary life end up around one table: relatives, colleagues, an old friend with his own views on everything. An hour later they are talking. Nobody noticed that this was the work of the person with 14: they dropped in a topic at the right moment, moved two people round, defused an argument with a joke before it flared up.

**The argument.** Two people pull in different directions: “let’s go to the sea” and “let’s go to the mountains”. 14 doesn’t work out who is right and doesn’t cut the holiday in half. It looks for a third option — a place that has both, or an order in which each gets what they want. A compromise is a concession. A blend is something new.
**The kitchen.** Someone cooks without a recipe, by eye, and it comes out delicious. That is not luck but a sense of proportion trained over years.

**The long haul.** A team has people who burn bright for a week and then go out, and someone who keeps the same stride all year. After a year, the second has done more. 14 is the arcanum of the marathon, not the sprint.

**After the storm.** People come to the person with 14 when things are bad: after a row, a redundancy, a break-up. They don’t hand out verdicts and don’t rush in to rescue — they bring the temperature back to normal. Wen writes about this card in almost the same words: it comes to “cool what was too hot, heat up what was too cold”, to “restore what was lost” and to “right what is wrong”.
All these scenes share one thing: 14 neither wins nor gives in — it joins.

Gender plays no part in calculating the matrix: a man and a woman born on the same day have the same numbers, and 14 means the same for both. The only difference is where a person is used to applying their sense of measure — in the family, at work, in arguments. The idea that 14 is a “feminine”, soft energy is a misunderstanding. Measure is needed by anyone who wants their strength not to break, and a calm man who doesn’t raise his voice and knows how to reach an agreement is none the weaker for it.

paragraphs: **Lukewarm water.** The most common one. A person blends so well that they themselves disappear from the blend. They give way in advance, before anyone has even asked, and then quietly resent that nobody took their wishes into account. On the outside there is peace and quiet; on the inside, a tally nobody has seen. A measure that leaves out one of the sides is no longer measure but dissolution.

**The seesaw.** Instead of proportion, an alternation of extremes: a month of strict routine, then a week of “oh, to hell with it all”. Each extreme looks like a correction of the last. This is hardening without tempering: a rule that is too rigid cracks, and the person is thrown to the opposite side. Matrix readings also file addictions here, and the logic is clear: an addiction is a measure that a person has handed over to something outside themselves.

**Haste.** 14 is the arcanum of time, and its shadow is impatience. Pushing a relationship that needs a year. Reworking a project that hasn’t had time to start working. Demanding a result of yourself in a week where a season is needed. Or the mirror image: “it’s not the right time yet” stretches out for years.

**The apothecary’s scales.** The search for the perfect proportion turns into perfectionism. Everything must be weighed to the gram, and nothing begins because the proportion isn’t perfect yet. A measure that paralyses is just another loss of measure.

paragraphs.h3: How to tell which way your 14 is working

ul: You can say what you want yourself before you offer a compromise.
Your working rhythm looks like a steady line, not a cardiogram.
After you make peace, the argument really is closed, not just postponed.
You can stop in the middle of a pleasure without bans and without guilt.
You notice when a matter needs waiting out and when it needs a push.

paragraphs: If most of these describe you, your 14 is working in the plus. If you recognised yourself in the traps, that is not a verdict but a pointer to where your measure has slipped.

sections.h2: Where 14 stands in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: The number at each point of the matrix comes from adding other numbers, and sums above 22 are reduced. Because of this, 14 lands at some points often, at others rarely, and at three never. The shares in the table are calculated over all birth dates from 1900 to 2026.

paragraphs: The calling card, point A, is calculated from the day of birth, and 14 stands there for everyone born on the 14th of any month. The calling card is the first minutes of an acquaintance, the layer of a person that others read fastest. With 14 in the calling card, a person enters a conversation without pressure, adjusts to the other person’s pace and lowers the temperature in the room. People say of them: “you feel calm with them”, “doesn’t fuss”, “a grown-up”. The flip side is a first impression that is too even: people don’t understand them straight away, and their politeness is sometimes mistaken for agreement. The same arcanum also leads the first decade of life: the age scale starts from the calling card, so for those born on the 14th the number 14 stands over the stretch from 0 to 10.

The family points are among the most frequent places for 14: the section on support and gifts of the family line comes up with this arcanum for 13.5% of people. In the spiritual lines, the father’s F and the mother’s G, 14 is a family value of measure: the family respected those who could reach agreement, never pushed things to extremes and kept the home in balance. In the material lines, H and I, it is a practice: thrift without stinginess, a reserve for hard times, an even household. The minus of a family 14 is the same as that of the arcanum in general: the rule “anything to avoid a quarrel”, handed down along with the peace.

In purpose, 14 is read by level. Personal: to learn your own measure — not to adjust to someone else’s middle, but to know your own proportion of work and rest, closeness and solitude. Social: to be the one who connects others — a translator between people, departments, generations. Planetary: what will outlive the person — a craft, a school, a tradition that needs years to ripen.

paragraphs.h3: The energy map: where 14 turns up most

paragraphs: The most frequent place for 14 is the chakra table: 44.2% of people have the arcanum there. Most often it stands in the emotions column of [manipura](/encyclopedia/chakra/manipura), and the reason is arithmetic. In the manipura row, physics and energy are the same number — the centre of the chart — and emotions are their sum. So everyone with 7 in the centre gets manipura 7-7-14: two Chariots added together make Temperance. That happens to roughly one person in nine. How speed and measure work in one chart is covered in the reading [The Chariot and Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/7-14). How to read the whole table is explained in the section [on the energy map](/encyclopedia/position/chakras).

In the reading by decades, 14 appears for 23% of people. The age scale goes round the eight outer points of the chart, ten years for each, and 14 can stand over any decade except the third: the stretch from 20 to 30 is led by the month of birth, and there are only twelve months. The stretch from 40 to 50 is led by the year of birth, so 14 is possible there only for those same people born between 1904 and 1940. A decade under 14 is a time not of dashes but of assembly: bringing back together what drifted apart, finding a rhythm that will last the years ahead. Don’t confuse it with the personal year: the year under arcanum 14 has [a reading of its own](/year/14).

paragraphs.h3: The karmic task and the tails

paragraphs: In the karmic task, point D, 14 stands for 1% of people, and all of them share the same combination: the karmic tail [6-20-14](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-20-14) and The Wheel of Fortune in the centre. This is not coincidence but arithmetic: when D equals 14, the other points of the tail are fixed. This tail is about love expressed through giving that silently waits for something back, and the 14 at its root teaches you to hold “giving” and “receiving” in the same hands. The second tail with this arcanum is [6-14-8](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-14-8), the rarest of all 26: here 14 stands in the middle. There are no other tails with 14, and it is never the first number of a tail. In all, 14 appears in the karmic tail of 1.2% of people.
Three positions are closed to 14 whatever the date of birth:

ul: **Spiritual task, point B.** It equals the month of birth, and there are twelve months.
**Entry of relationships and the tail, point M.** So 14 never opens either the relationship line or the karmic tail.
**Spiritual purpose.** The sum it is built from never gives 14, whatever the date.

paragraphs: If you were shown 14 at one of these points, either the calculation followed a different scheme, or it is a couple’s matrix, where the points are added up from two charts.

sections.h2: The talent of 14 and the careers that suit it
paragraphs: Talent in the matrix is read along a line of three points: the month of birth, the middle point of talent and the inner point K. 14 never falls on the month, but at the other two points it is frequent: the section “Profession and work you love” comes up with this arcanum for 11.3% of people.

The talent of 14 is a sense of proportion applied to work. Such a person sees how to join what others consider incompatible: two stubborn specialists, an old technology and a new task, a budget and a client’s dream. Wen reads this card in work questions in an unexpected way: “it isn’t that new skills need to be learned” — the skills you already have can be fused with a task they don’t seem meant for. For 14 in talent this is a good hint: your strong move is not yet another course but a new combination of what you can already do.
This gift becomes a profession wherever the result depends on proportion and time:

ul: **The craft of blending:** cooking, confectionery, baking, cheesemaking, perfumery, colour work, ceramics, glass — anywhere it matters how much of each thing goes in and how long to wait.
**Sound and colour:** sound engineer (the stage where the tracks are blended is called, fittingly, mixing), arranger, instrument tuner, restorer.
**People between sides:** translator, mediator, negotiator, HR specialist, project manager who brings departments together.
**Accompanying others:** teacher, mentor, counselling psychologist — work where another person’s pace matters, not only your own.
**The living and the slow:** gardening, landscape design, anything that grows in seasons rather than sprints.

paragraphs: Where the talent of 14 stalls: in work done in spurts. Constant crunches and “I needed it yesterday” rob this arcanum of its main advantage — an even stride. The second trap is the role of the eternal go-between, who gets other people’s conflicts but none of their own results. If you have spent years reconciling everyone but never done your own thing, the talent is working for others.

sections.h2: 14 in the money channel
paragraphs: The money line in the matrix is three points: the entry L, the middle point R2 (people call it “under the dollar”, after the sign on other schools’ charts; on ours it is labelled “Middle of the money line”) and the crossing with the relationship line, R. 14 can stand at any of them, and the section “Money in the destiny matrix” comes up with this arcanum for 11.4% of people.

A curious coincidence: when Waite listed this card’s divinatory meanings, he began with “Economy, moderation, frugality, management”. It is a rare case of an old list of meanings being directly about money — and it fits the matrix well.

**At the entry, point L,** 14 shows which action money begins with: joining. Income comes when a person brings sides together — client and contractor, product and buyer, two partners who would never have agreed on their own — or makes something where proportion decides everything.

**Under the dollar, at point R2,** 14 sets the condition for a stable income: an even pace. Money grows for whoever puts aside a little regularly, keeps spending in proportion to income and doesn’t chase quick money. Sharp moves — a loan for a hot idea, everything on one bet — work badly at this point.

**At the crossing, point R,** money and closeness affect each other. Here 14 wants a budget mixed honestly: not “everything shared” and not “each for themselves”, but an agreed proportion that both understand.

The minus of 14 in money shows in the same seesaw: a month of strict saving — and one day that eats everything saved. Or in dissolving: for years a person doesn’t raise their price because it feels “awkward”, and charges an average rate for above-average work.

What helps: a fixed share of income that is put aside at once rather than “whatever is left”; one spending rule instead of ten bans; a day’s pause before any big purchase. 14 decides best when the decision has been given time to steep.

sections.h2: 14 in relationships
paragraphs: In the relationships section, 14 appears for 10.2% of people. The entry of the relationship line, point M, is closed to this arcanum, so 14 turns up further along: in the middle of the line, “Under the heart”, at the crossing with money, or at the inner point of talent K, which also feeds into this section. 14 under the heart has [a reading of its own](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/14).

In love, 14 is pace and blending. A person with this arcanum doesn’t fall in love at a run and doesn’t break things off in one evening. They get close gradually and build what you could call a third thing: a shared household, a shared sense of humour, shared habits in which the two are mixed. It is calm beside them: rows don’t escalate, sharp corners get smoothed, and after a conflict the conversation returns to the matter at hand rather than to old grudges.

The weak spot is the same as in character: the wish for peace is stronger than the wish to be heard. 14 gives way before being asked, adapts to the partner’s schedule and tastes, says “I don’t mind, you choose”. For years this looks like perfect harmony, and then it turns out that one of them has been giving way all along while the other never even knew. A measure that contains only the partner is no measure.
What helps: name your own wish before looking for a compromise, not after; argue about the matter rather than smoothing it over; remember that in a good blend both parts can still be tasted.

sections.h2: 14 in compatibility: the couple’s matrix
paragraphs: Compatibility in the destiny matrix is a separate calculation. Under the common scheme, the matching points of two personal charts are added, the sums are reduced, and the resulting third matrix is read as a chart of the couple itself. Its points mean something different from those in a personal chart: the centre, for example, describes the overall atmosphere between the partners rather than the character of either one. Below is 14 in a couple’s matrix according to Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (The Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). This is her school and her practice, not a general canon.

**In the plus,** 14 makes a couple who argue with words rather than slammed doors: contradictions are settled by talking and compromise, and each understands the other’s needs. There is a balance between activity and quiet time together, and peace of mind is valued above things. Such a couple can be made up of very different people — by background, faith, habits — and the difference doesn’t drive them apart. With money there is no fuss: they spend according to income, don’t compete, and if they borrow, they pay it back.

**In the minus** — an imbalance visible from outside: one keeps giving way, and the other never gives it a thought. There is no common language and no sense of safety, there is a chill between the two; one of them shuts themselves off from family problems. In money, the same imbalance: one saves, the other spends, or one depends on the other.

The task of such a couple, according to Lisovskaya, is to reach agreement, not to rush to conclusions about the partner, not to offload their own fears onto them and not to try to control them. The method gives no compatibility percentages: 14 in a couple’s matrix speaks of what the couple needs to work on, not of whether the two people suit each other. 14 in the centre of a personal chart has [a reading of its own](/encyclopedia/position/center/14).

sections.h2: What helps 14 work in the plus

ol: **Your own first, then the shared.** Before you look for a compromise, name — at least to yourself — what you want. A blend without your part is made not of two ingredients but of one.

**Proportion instead of “equal shares”.** In an argument, ask not “how do we make it equal for everyone” but “how much of what does this need”. Sometimes the right proportion is ninety to ten, and that is more honest than half and half.
**Tempering instead of hardening.** If a rule keeps breaking — you hold on, you slip, you hold on again — it is too rigid. Soften it to something you can keep for a year, not a week.
**Time to steep.** Put off important decisions about money, moving or relationships for at least a day. This is not indecision: 14 thinks better when a thought has had time.

**A permitted extreme.** Keep one area where measure isn’t needed: loud music, spicy food, a Sunday of box sets until late at night. An extreme chosen in advance doesn’t build up and doesn’t break through as a seesaw. A measure with no room for an extreme becomes an extreme itself.
**Craft with your hands.** Cooking, mixing paints, mixing sound, pottering in the garden. 14 recovers in work where the proportion is visible and can be tasted.

sections.h2: Temperance in Waite’s deck: what the classic card shows
paragraphs: Next to this section is the card from the deck that Pamela Colman Smith drew in 1909 to Arthur Edward Waite’s design. Almost every symbol usually linked with 14 comes from here.

At the centre stands a winged angel in white. On its forehead is “the sign of the sun”, on its breast “the square and triangle of the septenary”, as Waite calls it: the square is four, the triangle three, together seven. Ouspensky, describing this sign, also placed a point inside the triangle: the triangle is the world of spirit, the square the visible world, the point the human soul. The angel holds two cups, and water flows diagonally between them. One foot stands in the water, the other on the bank. A path leads from the water towards the mountains, and above it is a radiance in which a crown can be made out. Yellow flowers grow by the water — they are usually called irises; Wen calls them lilies.

Waite himself explained the card like this. The angel is pouring “the essences of life from chalice to chalice”, and the one foot on the earth and the other on the waters show the dual nature of these essences. The whole scene, with the path towards the light, is in his words “some part of the Secret of Eternal Life, as it is possible to man in his incarnation”. The familiar readings — “changes in the seasons, perpetual movement of life” — he rejected outright. He thought the card’s name a matter of convention: it is “called Temperance fantastically, because, when the rule of it obtains in our consciousness, it tempers, combines and harmonises the psychic and material natures”. And describing older versions of the card, he remarked that the image “has no especial connexion with Temperance”, seeing in this an instance of “a meaning behind meaning” — the very thing that makes the tarot worth studying at all.

One more detail from Waite’s text: he refers to the angel as “he”, but at once adds that “the figure is neither male nor female”. A good answer to anyone who thinks of 14 as a “feminine” arcanum. The angel is also where 14 gets its “angelic” reputation in popular matrix readings.

The cups have been read in different ways. Ouspensky, who called the card “Time”, saw the past in one cup and the future in the other, and in the stream between them the present, which “flows both ways”; he admitted he could not tell from which cup into which the water was pouring. A hundred years later Wen asks the same question — does the water flow down “with gravity”, or up, “against the laws of physics”? — and sees in the cups the conscious and the unconscious, which the card reconciles.

The formula itself is older than Waite. In medieval art the virtue of Temperance was shown as a woman pouring liquid from one vessel into another — diluting wine with water. The early Italian cards of the fifteenth century kept to the same image.

sections.h2: The Temperance card in a tarot reading
paragraphs: If you came with a question about tarot rather than the matrix, this is how Temperance is read in a spread.

**Upright.** For Waite: “Economy, moderation, frugality, management, accommodation”. For Wen: internal balance and the need to “reconcile two contrasting elements”. In a love question she advises a single person to look at their own behaviour: the difficulties may come from an “internal imbalance”. To a couple, the card speaks of cooperation and of the time to temper “extreme emotions, such as anger, resentment, hostility”. In a career question, it says that new skills are not essential: it is enough to fit what you can already do to the task.

**Reversed.** Waite’s list is unexpected: “Things connected with churches, religions, sects, the priesthood, sometimes even the priest who will marry the Querent; also disunion, unfortunate combinations, competing interests.” Wen reads the reversed card more simply: temperance is needed but not applied — “excess, overflow”, an inability to stop in time.

There are no reversed arcana in the destiny matrix: a number calculated from a date doesn’t lie upside down. The plus and minus of 14 in a chart are not the position of a card but how a person uses their own sense of measure.

sections.h2: Neighbours in the deck and kindred arcana
paragraphs: The meaning of 14 shows clearly through its neighbours. Before it stands Death (13) — an ending after which the old form does not return. After it comes The Devil (15), the arcanum of passion, temptation and attachment. Temperance between them is like the pause between two blows: after an ending, not to throw yourself into the first extreme that comes along, but to make a new blend out of what is left. If 15 is measure lost, 14 is measure held. How these arcana work within one chart is covered in the readings [Death and Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/13-14) and [Temperance and The Devil](/encyclopedia/combination/14-15).

The second family of 14 is the virtues. Three cards of the deck grew out of the classical list of virtues: Justice, Strength and Temperance. In the Marseilles order the matrix uses, they stand at equal steps — 8, 11, 14. Waite swapped Strength and Justice, but the step stayed the same. The fourth virtue, prudence, is missing from the deck, and where it went is still debated.
All three are about measure, but different kinds of it:

ul: **[Justice (8)](/encyclopedia/arcanum/8)** — measure on the outside: decision, responsibility, an honest account. Wen draws the line in exactly this way: 8 is external balance, 14 internal. Together — in the reading [Justice and Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/8-14).

**[Strength (11)](/encyclopedia/arcanum/11)** — the measure of force: passion and stubbornness not suppressed but tamed. Together — in the reading [Strength and Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/11-14).
**Temperance (14)** — the measure of a blend: not one thing defeating the other, but both becoming a third.

paragraphs: And one more comparison from Wen: [The Moon (18)](/encyclopedia/arcanum/18) speaks of the repressed — what a person does not want to see in themselves — while Temperance is about how the repressed and the conscious begin to come to terms.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: The card’s symbolism and divinatory meanings — A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, reissued 1922): the image and its meaning from Part II, the meanings in a spread from Part III.
The modern reading — Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015), the section on Key 14.
The name “Time” and the reading of the cups — P. D. Ouspensky, Simvoly Taro (The Symbolism of the Tarot, 1912).
The couple’s matrix — Yu. Lisovskaya, Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (The Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024), the chapter on the 14th energy.

Positions and shares — calculated with Natalia Ladini’s classic destiny matrix scheme, running through every birth date from 1 January 1900 to 2026. How the calculation works is explained on the page [about the method](/method).
The readings of positions are our adaptation of the card’s meaning to the role of each point: a way to understand yourself, not a prediction of events.

items.title: The Devil
items.short: passion and matter: gives a powerful pull and the bill for it
meaning: The fifteenth arcanum is attraction. Fifteen in the destiny matrix means a person is driven by strong, bodily wanting: a pull towards money, towards another person, towards power, towards taste, towards having things at all. This is the most earthly of the major energies — it does not reason and does not wait, it pulls you towards the object like gravity. That is where the power of this number comes from, and its price.

The main engine here is appetite, and appetite is also the main question. The same wanting works as fuel and as a trap: while it belongs to you, you take and you build; the moment it becomes the master, it takes you. The inner conflict of the arcanum is not between wanting and not wanting, but between “I have a desire” and “the desire has me”. The number itself never draws that line — a person draws it again every time.

To carry this arcanum is to live with a constant inflow of force and a constant temptation. Inside there is heat, magnetism, the feeling that you can get what you want if you really want it; and beside it a quiet current that drifts you back to whatever already holds you. People notice someone like this: the fifteenth has a dense presence, others follow and believe. Emptiness and half-measures are unbearable — where there is no taste and no thrill, a dull tension builds up.

Fifteen at its strongest stays the owner of its own pull rather than its servant: it turns hunger into work, magnetism into the ability to lead, and takes what it wants without growing into it for good. The weak one is ruled by the pull: the thing wanted becomes a leash, and all the force goes into holding on to what is already held. The difference is not in how much a person wants, but in which of the two is in charge.

Next to its neighbours the fifteenth differs by temperature. The fourteenth, Temperance, dilutes and balances and waits for the right proportion — The Devil thickens and takes at once, because measure bores it. The sixteenth, The Tower, is the collapse of what was held for too long; the fifteenth is exactly what builds up the attachment that The Tower later brings down. The Devil is about the chain and its sweetness, The Tower about the moment the chain breaks.

in_positions.character: A strong presence and an obvious pull: people notice this person and are drawn to them. They know what they want, see where others are weak, and know how to use it — sometimes gently, sometimes not.
in_positions.comfort: Pleasure is what refills this centre: taste, the body, money, a real passion for the work. Self-denial and constant limits never settle this centre — they store up tension until it breaks out.
in_positions.profession: The strong side here is reading other people’s motives and their material interest. Sales, negotiation, finance and any task that needs a firm grip and a precise read of what people want. The risk is swapping mutual benefit for pressure, for the thrill of the game, or for control at any price. The Devil’s best offer does not hide the wanting behind pretty words: the interest of both sides is named out loud, and the gain is confirmed by the result.
in_positions.realisation: Everything here leads into matter: to earn, to build, to get and to keep. Spiritual talk with nothing to show for it bores this person; meaning arrives through the body, through things, through what has been achieved.
in_positions.karma40: The fifteenth arcanum in the age lens shows ties that turn into dependence. They can form around people, around pleasures or around work, and the new answer is to take the controls back.
in_positions.resources: The resource channel is desire. While the person wants openly and feels no shame about it, the channel stays open; the moment they start explaining that they need very little, it shuts. Desire here is a working tool, not a sin: being ashamed of it closes the entrance faster than any competitor.
in_positions.family_gifts: From the family line came a grip and the knack of surviving in hard conditions. Someone rose from nothing by means that were not the cleanest — that force is in the person, and owning it is more honest than hiding it. The grip is inherited; the price once paid for it does not have to be.
in_positions.soul_tasks: The soul’s work here is about freedom. The test is simple: next to this person, does another one breathe easier, or do they slowly lose their own will? The answer decides where the force of the arcanum goes.
in_positions.past_lives: The automatic script is to hold and to be held. The pull is real: this person knows how to want and how to get, and life beside them is never bland. Relationships are built through power, money and obligations, and they are hard to break even when everything is bad. Call the bond by its real name: what exactly holds it — feeling, habit or calculation.
in_positions.purpose: Taking material things and making something useful of them is the task: a business, money, production, a hand to those who are stuck. Such people see another’s grip straight through, because they know the mechanism from the inside.
in_positions.money: What gets paid for is drive and an eye for profit: trade, services, property, everything bodily and pleasant. There can be a lot of money here, and the weak spot is spending that eats the earnings faster than they arrive. Turn the wanting into a budget: how much is needed, for what exactly, and what you are ready to give up — without pretending that money leaves you cold.
in_positions.money40: Mature money of the fifteenth arcanum rests on what is formalised: property, shares, income from assets, not spoken promises. The powerful pull towards matter finally takes shape with experience — what used to burn up in bets now goes on paper. The taste for a gamble does not leave on its own: a bet stays a bet at twenty and at fifty, and the calendar does not cancel it. Check whose name the things you use every day are in, and put the papers in order.
in_positions.relations: Passion here is real and strong, and it is also the main risk: jealousy, control, freedom traded for comfort. Good relationships for this arcanum are the ones where both could leave and stay by their own choice. A wish said out loud is easy to test: if it matches the other’s, that is closeness; if it does not, it is a deal.
in_positions.parents_children: Generosity in this family always came together with holding on: they gave a lot and did not let go. It works the same way further down — liveliness, presents and attention reach the youngest along with too much control. It helps to hand over the right to their own decisions earlier than you feel like doing it: this arcanum loves to keep hold.
in_positions.ancestry: A theme of debt and unfreedom runs through the family line: someone was in bondage, in dependence, under another’s power. The task is to live your own life without it and not pass it on. Review one arrangement that has long rested on a sense of duty, and name the condition under which taking part stays voluntary.
in_positions.body_resource: Desire lights the Devil up in seconds and burns through the whole evening just as fast: the intensity here is both the fuel and the main leak. Things hold together when the strong wanting comes after the work is done rather than instead of it: first the task closed, then the loud evening. The thin spot is the habit of always picking the most intense option, until the quiet ones stop registering at all. A practical test — put off one automatic choice for ten minutes and write down what changed in the decision.
in_positions.chakras: The Devil: what this level holds — passion and matter. In resource you see the energy of wanting that carries a thing all the way to money; in overload, an attachment that starts giving you orders. To even it out, keep checking who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.rest: Recovery comes through the body and through taste: the sea, good food, a steam bath, a massage, good company. A dry timetable of rest gets rejected by this arcanum, which always finds a way to break it. The limit has to be named in advance: otherwise by morning the pleasure turns into a bill paid in tiredness.
in_positions.loops: The same loop repeats: wanted it, got it, got tied to it, tore free with losses. The way out is to decide in advance what you are paying with, and to hold that decision when the wanting grows stronger.
in_positions.years: The Devil’s ten years push material things to the front: earnings, purchases, strong ties, strong temptations. The pull towards matter works for the person as long as they know the figure of their obligations by heart and check it against reality. Spending in these years is usually higher than they notice, and intensity passes easily for proof of being right. Once a quarter, recount the obligations taken on and keep the right to walk out of a deal that is not working.
in_positions.day: Arcanum “The Devil” · A · The first impression is built around one theme — passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. At full strength the person knows how to want and to get material things; under strain they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. The image turns into a steady reputation when they manage to check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.month: Arcanum “The Devil” · B · The inborn spiritual task switches on by itself: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. So the person may not count it as a gift that they know how to want and to get material things; the other side shows when they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. The mature task of this position is to check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.year: Arcanum “The Devil” · C · The material task carries the theme “passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it” from intention into result. Their strong side is visible in what they do: they know how to want and to get material things; out of balance they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. This position is lived not by a promise but by the readiness to check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.mission: Arcanum “The Devil” · D · This is not a punishment but a story that keeps coming back: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. The grown-up answer starts where the person knows how to want and to get material things, and the old circle starts with the opposite: they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. Breaking the repeat takes one concrete decision: check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.center: Arcanum “The Devil” · E · At the centre of the chart it is easier to be yourself through the theme: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. On their own footing the person knows how to want and to get material things; losing the centre shows in the way they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. What brings them back is not distraction but action — to check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.father_line: Arcanum “The Devil” · F · The spiritual male line keeps a principle: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. The strong side of the inheritance shows like this: the person knows how to want and to get material things; the heavy side of the script is that they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. Taking the force of the line without its hardness means checking who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.mother_line: Arcanum “The Devil” · G · The spiritual female line keeps the rule of the house: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. In the supporting version the person knows how to want and to get material things; in the tangled one they repeat something else — they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. Rewriting the rule while keeping its value comes down to a choice: check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.descendants: Arcanum “The Devil” · H · Here the family principle becomes an act: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. In its reliable form the person knows how to want and to get material things; the automatic one is that they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. A new continuation of the male line begins with the skill of checking who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.inheritance: Arcanum “The Devil” · I · Here the values of the family enter everyday life: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. The resource appears when the person knows how to want and to get material things; the usual tilt is that they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. Making the inheritance a support rather than a duty takes the readiness to check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.comfort_west: Arcanum “The Devil” · J · The outer portrait A joins the centre E through the theme “passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it”. If the passage is free, the person knows how to want and to get material things; if the role argues with the inner state, they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. Bringing the outer and the inner together takes one decision: check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.comfort_north: Arcanum “The Devil” · K · The talent on the line B–P–K takes shape: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. The mature gift shows in the way the person knows how to want and to get material things; trying to earn recognition leads to them falling into dependence — on people, on things, on work. The talent takes its form when they manage to check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.comfort_east: Arcanum “The Devil” · L · The money line opens with the theme “passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it”. This is not a promise of income but a way in: at their best the person knows how to want and to get material things, out of balance they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. To turn the impulse into a steady business, keep checking who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.comfort_south: Arcanum “The Devil” · M · At the fork between relationships and the karmic tail this comes out: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. The first reaction helps closeness when the person knows how to want and to get material things, and it starts the old script when they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. What keeps them off the circle is a pause in which they can check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.love_middle: Arcanum “The Devil” · R1 · Attraction becomes the main thing — bodily, strong, sometimes stronger than common sense. Living passion holds a couple together where agreements alone would have emptied out long ago. Hurt and desire mix into a knot with no way out: hard together, impossible apart, and talking gets replaced by working out who owes whom. Take important decisions a day after making up, not on the same night.
in_positions.harmony: Arcanum “The Devil” · spiritual · The personal and the social levels are joined by the theme “passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it”. Agreement with themselves is felt when the person knows how to want and to get material things; the inner argument comes back when they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. Tying the two levels into one direction takes the readiness to check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.planetary: Arcanum “The Devil” · planetary · Past a personal biography reaches the theme “passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it”, out beyond one life story. The contribution becomes visible to many when the person knows how to want and to get material things; the scale stays a nice idea if they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. Starting from real influence rather than a loud role takes one decision: check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.purpose_personal: Arcanum “The Devil” · personal · With no audience around, the person would choose the theme: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. Being true to themselves shows in the way they know how to want and to get material things; stepping away from their task shows in the way they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. This position comes alive when they manage to check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.
in_positions.purpose_social: Arcanum “The Devil” · social · Other people can lean on the theme: passion and matter: it gives a powerful pull and the bill that comes with it. In shared work they are most useful when they know how to want and to get material things; the role stops working when they fall into dependence — on people, on things, on work. Steady use instead of an image comes from one concrete choice: check who makes the decisions in the pair of “me and my desire”.

The test is simple: can you walk out of the work and out of the bond calmly; if not, this is no longer about desire.
